Today, we’re sharing early progress on ChatGPT for Teens, including how teens are using its learning tools, along with new ways for teens to study and prepare for college.
L35: ChatGPT’s 1.2 billion users span many countries, communities and backgrounds. That reach makes it especially important to build tools that help young people with different resources and opportunities learn and prepare for their futures.
L36: ## What we’re seeing so far
L37: 
L38: ChatGPT for Teens is designed to help young people learn, think critically and deepen their understanding. As ChatGPT for Teens became available to more teens globally, those with access sent about 2.7 million more learning-related messages on average than those who didn’t have it yet.
L39: Once enrolled, teens use ChatGPT for Teens’ learning tools at scale. The most selected conversation starter prompts are “ask questions to develop my ideas,” “give feedback on my draft,” and “help me check my evidence.” In one week, nearly 1.2 million teens used Learning Visualizations to better understand math and science concepts, and more than 180,000 used Study Mode for step-by-step learning support.
L40: ChatGPT for Teens includes cite9†built-in reminders to encourage teens to take breaks. On average, teens spend under 15 minutes a day on ChatGPT. While less than 2% of teens spend more than three consecutive hours on ChatGPT, in almost half of teen conversations with a break reminder, teens took a break or ended their conversation within five minutes.
L41: These usage patterns remain well below the cite10†publicly reported⁠(opens in a new window)†www.apa.org average of 5 hours for teen social media usage, and reflect a different kind of experience: ChatGPT is designed for learning, building, and creativity, rather than passive scrolling. Among teens with sessions longer than three consecutive hours, over 80% had at least one prompt related to learning.
L42: These early signs are encouraging and we’ll continue to evaluate the experience and learn from teens, families and educators to improve ChatGPT for Teens.
L43: ## Introducing College Planner to help teens prepare for what’s next
L44: 
L45: Hundreds of thousands of US teens use ChatGPT each week to plan for college. They’re using it to plan applications, track deadlines, research schools and understand financial aid.
L46: That’s why we’ll soon be adding College Planner to ChatGPT for Teens. We’re designing it to help students manage the practical steps of applying to college, without taking over the personal work of figuring out where they want to apply. Students have different levels of access to support with college applications. Our goal is to make help more accessible, regardless of financial circumstances, alongside guidance from counselors, advisers, and families.
L47: College Planner brings together application requirements, deadlines, tasks, and financial-aid steps for schools on a student’s list in one plan. Students applying to several colleges can return to it to update their progress, use the timeline to plan ahead and see what’s left to do. They can also ask ChatGPT questions along the way, from what a requirement means to how to get started.
L48: By bringing these steps together, we aim to save students and families time and make a stressful process feel more manageable.
L49: We’re designing the initial US experience for high-school students in grades 10–12 who are planning to attend a four-year college. We plan to bring College Planner to students in more countries and expand support to two-year colleges, technical colleges, trade schools and more over time.
L50: 
L51: College Planner also helps students figure out how to pay for college. They can get help understanding financial aid requirements, track each school’s aid deadlines, and explore scholarships and fee waivers.
L52: Keeping track of an application is only one part of preparing for college. Many students also need someone to help them make sense of their options. Alongside College Planner, we’re supporting cite11†College Advising Corps⁠(opens in a new window)†collegeadvisingcorps.org , a nonprofit that places recent college graduates as advisers in under-resourced high schools to help students navigate the path to higher education.
L53: OpenAI’s contribution will help the organization expand into new states and create an AI fellowship program. Through the fellowship, advisers across participating states will test and share practical ways to use AI to help more students navigate the path to college. AI can help students manage application and enrollment tasks. Advisers can help them consider their options and decide what to do next.
L54: > “For students navigating the college application process, an unanswered question about a form, deadline, or fee can feel like a closed door. College Advising Corps advisers help students work through those moments with confidence. We see promise in College Planner as a tool that can help students prepare for those conversations, stay on track, and continue moving toward a college that is affordable and aligned with their goals.”
L55: 
L56: —Ekaterina Struett, CEO, College Advising Corps
L57: ## Supporting Boston Children’s Hospital to engage teens
L58: When we cite8†introduced ChatGPT for Teens , we committed to keep improving the experience. We’re supporting cite12†Boston Children’s Hospital’s Digital Wellness Lab⁠(opens in a new window)†digitalwellnesslab.org and its independent cite13†Student Advisory Council⁠(opens in a new window)†digitalwellnesslab.org over the next three years to learn directly from young people about how AI fits into their lives and to give teenagers a meaningful stake at the table as AI is being designed.
L59: For the 2026–27 school year, the Lab will bring together ~22 students across two tracks: ~12 students ages 14–18 working on digital wellbeing projects in their communities and ~10 students ages 16–20, focused on building AI chatbots and emerging technology. These students will work alongside researchers and clinicians on digital wellbeing and AI projects. Students in the AI track will test tools and recommend changes based on how they use AI in learning and their personal lives.
L60: We expect to seek feedback on teen safety defaults, parental controls and notifications and AI literacy.
L61: Teens should play a central role in developing the tools that will shape their future. Teens will test tools and develop recommendations for the people building them. Our aim is to bring those recommendations into product and model decisions early and to report back to students on what we change and why. This advisory board will give them a direct voice in that work and share their insights and recommendations to help the wider industry build better tools for young people.
L62: > “Young people bring critical insights and knowledge that adults don’t have. They see what works, what fails, and what needs to change.”
L63: 
L64: —Dr. Michael Rich, Founder & Director and Cori Stott, Executive Director, Digital Wellness Lab, April 2026.
L65: ## More ways for teens to study with flashcards and quizzes
L66: 
L67: We heard from students that photographing and uploading their notes to ChatGPT can take hours. We’re making it easier for students to turn their notes into study materials like flashcards and quizzes.
L68: 
L69: With continuous, multi-photo capture, students can photograph multiple pages of notes and automatically combine them into a single PDF, ready to upload to ChatGPT. This is available on iOS, and we’re working to bring it to Android.
L70: We’re also adding flashcards to help teens practice what they’re learning. A student preparing for a biology test, for example, can upload class notes or choose a topic, and ChatGPT can turn the material into cards to review. They can mark the cards they know, return to the ones they missed or shuffle the deck for another round. Decks are saved in a teen’s Library, so it’s easy to pick up where they left off.
L71: Students can also ask ChatGPT to pull up the flashcards and create a scheduled task to practice them.
L72: Alongside flashcards, we’ve made it easier to create Quizzes in ChatGPT. Students can now upload their notes to turn them into interactive quizzes, and ChatGPT is better at recognizing when you want a quiz and creating one directly in chat.
L73: 
L74: We’ll keep learning from teens, families and educators, checking how protections work in practice and sharing what we learn as ChatGPT for Teens evolves.

articles.title: 诺奖经济学家给出判断：10年內仅5%工作会被AI真正取代
articles.text:
快科技10月8日消息，微软AI负责人苏莱曼在社交平台转发了诺贝尔经济学奖得主阿西莫格鲁的研究观点，打破不少人担心AI会大面积裁员的焦虑。
按照这份估算，未来10年真正被AI顶替掉的工作大概只有5%。
很多人不知道，理论技术层面AI其实有能力搞定20%的工作内容。可理想和现实中间隔着企业落地的门槛，就算AI在实验室测试效果很惊艳，搬到真实公司环境，往往会出现各种水土不服。
举两个很现实的例子，AI写出来的代码，工程师要花大量时间排查、修改；AI给出的医学影像参考，医生也没法直接拿来就用，依旧要结合自身经验重新判断。
软件迭代飞快，但企业改造流程、员工适应工具都需要时间，这就大大拖慢AI替代岗位的速度。阿西莫格鲁本人也特意说明，5%只是估算数字，不是板上钉钉的结果。
有意思的是，苏莱曼自己之前也说过，律师、会计、项目经理这类白领，不少工作内容12?18个月就能交给AI处理。
后来他专门做了解释，他说的是零散工作任务，不是把一整个岗位彻底取消。AI更多是帮人减负提速，而不是直接把人换掉。
这位诺奖学者还提到另一个关键点，不要过度神话AI对经济的拉动效果。就算AI工具大范围铺开，未来10年给整体生产效率带来的提升也比较有限，并不会出现想象里面经济爆炸式增长的局面。
当然这不代表大家可以完全躺平。AI会接管写初稿、整理表格这类重复琐事，岗位的工作内容会发生改变。从业者需要学会和AI配合，把精力放在需要判断力、沟通、复杂决策的部分。
网上一直有两种声音，一部分人恐慌AI会大批裁员，另一部分人鼓吹AI马上颠覆所有行业。
这份研究相当于给出一个折中视角，AI会改变工作，但短时间不会大规模淘汰岗位。最终实际会发展成什么样，还要看企业实际落地推进的节奏。

articles.title: HouseholdBench: Evaluating Large Language Models as Predictors of Household Economic Behavior
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.07563v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have the potential to meet a key goal in economics: a quantitative model of household decision making, across a variety of settings. Yet existing evaluations cover few surveys and outcomes, and do not study how households adjust to changing economic conditions. We introduce a new evaluation, HouseholdBench, which unites 6 U.S. household surveys and 32 prediction tasks spanning numeric, categorical and probabilistic outcomes, related to consumption, income, labor, expectations, and housing. Using past behavior, demographics and macroeconomic conditions, the tasks test whether LLMs predict behavior, including how households adjust to changes in various policies. We evaluate 13 proprietary and open-weight LLMs against a no-change baseline and a gradient-boosted tree model. Most LLMs outperform the no-change baseline, including for policy response tasks -- with the best model lowering error for numeric outcomes by 12.2%. Across most tasks, gradient-boosted trees rank first; leading proprietary LLMs approach their performance, but open-weight models lag. LLMs exhibit systematic over- and underprediction across different tasks. We identify methods that enable a 4 billion parameter open-weight model to match proprietary models' performance: fine-tuning and aggregating 16 predictions per observation. Improvements generalize to policy-response tasks, which are excluded from fine-tuning. We release our datasets, code, and leaderboard on our website: https://jn-huang.github.io/householdbench

articles.title: DRAM涨声再起！南亚科计划涨价：涨幅最高达20%
articles.text:
快科技10月7日消息，据媒体报道，中国台湾存储厂商南亚科近期已通知客户，将再度上调DRAM合约价格，最高涨幅可达20%。对于这一消息，南亚科方面表示“不予置评”。业内分析认为，随着南亚科启动新一轮合约价上调，企业整体经营状况有望持续向好。
众所周知，今年第三季度扎堆发布的多款旗舰手机，已经开启新一轮涨价潮。以iPhone为例，最新推出的iPhone 18 Pro和iPhone 18 Pro Max，起售价均上涨了1000元，而存储芯片价格的持续走高，正是涨价的核心诱因之一。
调研机构TrendForce发布的报告显示，2026年第四季度DRAM合约价格将延续上涨趋势，常规DRAM预计环比上涨10%至15%。
涨价的核心原因来自供需结构性失衡，AI算力建设拉动服务器DRAM与HBM需求持续走高，存储大厂优先把先进制程产能投向高利润的服务器存储产品，从而挤压了PC、手机所用消费级DRAM的产能。
与此同时，原厂维持保守扩产策略，行业库存处于低位，供给弹性不足，进一步加剧了价格上涨的压力。受涨价影响，有的厂商开始精简产品矩阵，砍掉了Ultra手机，以减少产品线冗余。
此举能够在一定程度上控制研发与备货成本，目前来看，内存成本压力短期难以缓解，预计后续新品定价会继续抬升。对消费者而言，购机门槛也将进一步抬高。

articles.title: ChatGPT rated "unacceptable risk" for teens after parental alerts failed during suicide conversations
articles.text:

articles.title: 华为徐直军：昇腾950超节点国内都不够用 没计划全面出海
articles.text:
快科技10月7日消息，在华为全联接大会结束之后，华为对外公开了徐直军与媒体的交流内容，围绕新推出的昇腾950超节点产品、国内算力市场格局以及芯片自主发展方向作出解读。
昇腾950超节点依托华为全新的Peerium计算架构打造，这套架构跳出传统主从模式，能够把成千上万颗处理器整合，如同单台计算机协同运转，实现计算、存储、网络资源的对等互联，以此适配大模型训练所需的海量算力需求。
谈及海外市场布局，徐直军表示，现阶段昇腾950超节点的产能还无法充分满足国内的旺盛需求，因此华为并没有将该产品大规模推向海外市场的打算。
虽然部分海外国家对这套算力产品有着较强需求，华为也开展了相关测试与少量供货，但对外输出的规模十分有限。
结合华为方面统计的市场数据，昇腾系列产品在国内市场的占比已经超过英伟达。他也坦言，想要获取对手准确的市场份额统计数据本身存在不小难度。
在芯片产业发展层面，徐直军认为，推进芯片产业自主可控是国内发展的必然方向。作为人口众多的工业大国，国内各行各业生产生活都深度依赖芯片，行业不能长期面临芯片供给被外部左右的局面。
即便当前国产芯片的技术水平和国际顶尖水准仍存有差距，但稳定可控的供货能力有着极高价值。面向未来，华为相信国内半导体全产业链实现自给自足的目标终将实现，这也是产业与企业共同前行的重要方向。

articles.title: 10 年内预估仅 5%：诺奖经济学家背书，AI 不会大规模抢走你的饭碗
articles.text:
IT之家 10 月 8 日消息，微软 AI 首席执行官穆斯塔法 · 苏莱曼（Mustafa Suleyman）于 10 月 6 日在 X 平台发布推文，援引诺贝尔经济学奖得主达龙 · 阿西莫格鲁（Daron Acemoglu）的预测称，未来 10 年内仅有约 5% 的人类工作会被人工智能取代。
IT之家查询公开资料，阿西莫格鲁是当代颇具影响力的经济学家之一，主要研究政治经济学、经济发展、制度、技术变迁与收入不平等。
他于 2024 年和西蒙 · 约翰逊（Simon Johnson）、詹姆斯 · 罗宾逊（James A. Robinson）共同获得诺贝尔经济学奖，获奖理由是“关于制度如何形成及其如何影响繁荣的研究”。
本次转发的文章于今年 7 月发表在《人文主义评论》（The Humanist Review）创刊号上，阿西莫格鲁估算，从技术上来看，AI 可以自动化约 20% 的工作，但受企业采纳速度限制，10 年内实际自动化比例仅约 5%。他坦言这一数字“诚然只是一个估计值”。
阿西莫格鲁指出，当前 AI 模型在编写代码、放射诊断等实验室场景中表现卓越，但企业在真实环境中部署同类工具时效果逊色。工程师需花费大量时间调试 AI 生成代码，医生难以将专业知识与 AI 工具有效结合，导致结果未达预期。模型进步速度快于企业可用工具的成熟度。
苏莱曼今年 2 月曾对《金融时报》表示，律师、会计师、项目经理等白领岗位的“大部分任务”将在 12 至 18 个月内实现自动化。6 月他在播客中澄清，此言指“任务”而非“岗位”，AI 仅让工作完成更快，不意味职位消失。

articles.title: Surface与Macbook正面交锋
articles.text:
微软部门副总Brett Ostrum接受采访时称，微软上一次推出基于高通ARM处理器的Copilot Plus PC实际上是为了对抗大众级Macbook Air，公司当然也想撼动Macbook Pro的行业地位，但苦于SoC能效落后：
“我们知道，当时的芯片无法达到Macbook Pro的水平”，Brett称。
于是，当英伟达私下展示某款在研芯片的强大性能时，微软对此很感兴趣，双方一拍即合：“能与Macbook Pro正面交锋意义重大，英伟达对于我们来说是天作之合”，Brett表示。双方密切合作了多年，最终促成Surface Laptop Ultra闪亮登场。
Surface Laptop Ultra与Macbook Pro同样采用CNC一体成型加工工艺，具备超大触控板，巧克力键盘，高端屏幕，24GB机型起价2600美元，128GB顶配机型需支付5900美元。
内置的RTX Spark SoC专为本地AI负载设计，可运行2800亿参数密实模型，实现Token自由，更无敏感信息泄漏之虞。与CPU集成的英伟达GPU凭借统一内存技术可轻松处理Blender 3D、Photoshop Premiere等图形负载，当然也能玩游戏。
媒体人士获邀在展示机上运行新近发布的《战争机器：事变日》，主观感受极为流畅，即便笔记本供电方式由市电切换为电池也没有可察觉的性能下降。
为了进一步向Mac机看齐，除内部结构如Macbook般规整外，微软设计团队还煞费苦心地为其设计了磁吸充电口——这是全行业首款运用磁吸原理的USB-C接口：
Surface对微软而言并非仅是一门生意，它还负责向合作伙伴展示Windows平台的实力。微软通过Surface在触控板、显示屏、手写笔支持、性能与设计领域推动了行业进步，如果微软自己都不上心，Win本与Mac本之间的差距会越来越大。
Surface Laptop Ultra即日开启预定，本月16号出货。入门型号仅售2600美元，配备15寸mini-LED屏幕、大尺寸触控板、三个机身USB-C口（含磁吸口），5120CU的18核RTX Spark以及24GB统一内存，目标客户是视频编辑、照片创作、数据处理、3D建模人员与游戏玩家。

articles.title: Rust 实现渐进渲染：谷歌官宣 Chrome 155 浏览器支持解码 JPEG XL 图片格式
articles.text:
IT之家 10 月 8 日消息，谷歌开发者博客于 10 月 6 日发布博文，宣布在谷歌 Chrome 155 浏览器中，解码支持 JPEG XL (.jxl) 图片格式。
官方介绍称 JPEG XL 是一种新一代图片格式，旨在满足现代 Web 开发者和摄影师的需求。与 JPEG 相比，它可提供 30-50% 的压缩率，支持无损压缩、内置 HDR 支持、无损 JPEG 转码等。
谷歌开发者团队建议用户同时尝试 AVIF 和 JPEG XL。其中 AVIF 凭借极高的压缩效率、丰富的功能集和广泛的浏览器支持，适合“带宽敏感、加载速度关键、图片数量大”的场景；而 JPEG XL 最适合用于高保真或无损压缩，尤其是摄影图像，或者需要细粒度渐进式解码的情况。
此前 Firefox 浏览器展示的效果图片
谷歌团队还分享了一段视频，介绍了 JPEG XL 的渐进式解码，示例图像完整文件为 146.7 KB，下载数 kB 后，用户已可辨认图像主体。IT之家附上相关视频如下：
安全方面，谷歌表示图片解码器是任何现代网络浏览器中最关键且最容易受到定向攻击的攻击面之一。它们直接从网络处理复杂且不受信任的二进制结构，并在渲染器进程中运行。
从历史上看，使用 C++ 等非内存安全型语言编写的解码器容易出现越界读取、堆溢出和释放后使用 bug 等漏洞。为了从源头上消除这些安全风险，谷歌集成了 jxl-rs，这是 JPEG XL 解码器的纯 Rust 实现。
为维持运行速度，谷歌在解码器中采用安全的 SIMD 指令，并构建 SIMD 抽象层。Chrome 还整合了 jxl-rs 的性能优化。谷歌称，团队通过 AI 审查和模糊测试检查 jxl-rs 实现。相关测试在开发过程中未发现内存安全问题。
相关阅读：
《Rust 实现渐进渲染：火狐 Firefox 浏览器 157 将开放支持 JPEG XL 图片格式》

articles.title: Hybrid Latent Attention for Looped Language Models
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.07940v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Looped language models apply the same stack of layers T times to each token, which deepens the model without adding parameters but multiplies its key-value (KV) cache by T. The larger cache limits how many sequences a GPU can decode at once and slows each decoding step, which reads the whole cache. We propose Hybrid Latent Attention (HLA), which keeps exact keys and values within a sliding window of W recent tokens and stores each older token as a compact latent that the query of each loop reads directly, without reconstructing keys and values. We uptrain HLA on Ouro looped models (T=4) with 1.4B and 2.6B parameters, keeping the pretrained weights frozen and training only the added parameters to reproduce the original attention. The cache shrinks by 10.7x per token, fitting 4.0-8.8x as many concurrent sequences per GPU, and decoding throughput improves by 2.5x at 1K-token contexts and by up to 7.4x at 16K. HLA retains over 97% of the original accuracy on math, knowledge and reasoning benchmarks, and 96-100% on long-context retrieval up to 16K tokens. After supervised fine-tuning, it performs on par with the fine-tuned original model on competition-level math.

articles.title: 你看到的垃圾广告 压根就不是拍给人看的
articles.text:
相信很多人依旧清晰记得2007 年底，步步高音乐手机拍的一条广告。
墨尔本海边，一身白衣的宋慧乔戴着耳机听歌，整条广告只有一段女声哼唱，可看完你就记住了：步步高能让你享受音乐。
十几年后它被搬上视频平台，评论区一片“满满的回忆”。
那个年代，能让人记十几年的广告并不少见。
2000 年前后，李玟那句“好迪真好，大家好才是真的好”，配着《Di Da Di》在央视播了好几年，我这么一提，你大概已经哼起“嘀嗒嘀”了。
后来德芙的一句“纵享丝滑”，把一块巧克力卖出了丝绸的手感。
2008 年，益达拍了条超市篇，一句“你的益达”，让郭碧婷第一次被大家记住，这句台词也被网友记到了今天。
那时上得了电视的广告，谈不上个个是神作，但起码算件作品：观众看完记住了牌子，也记住了这个牌子是什么调性。
可现在打开手机，你刷到的广告完全是另一副样子。
你可能刷到过这样的视频：画面像是养殖场的监控，一道闪电劈下来，十几头猪当场倒地。你还在琢磨这是哪儿的新闻，画面一切，成了一款游戏的广告。
那段监控一眼能看出 AI 做的，跟游戏八竿子打不着，它的目的只有一个：让你不要在 2 秒内划走。
网盘推广也爱这么干，配音和文字讲的是产品活动，画面放的却是毫不相干的剧情。
这种骗你不要划走的广告，还算是轻的。
《疯狂水世界》的广告，这大半年你大概没少刷到。
剧情翻来覆去就一个路数：主角处处受欺负，终于捞到一台海水过滤器，住进高级庇护所，又嫌太小，再去捞电鳗发电机，最后一句“疯狂水世界启动”，切进“游戏画面”。
广告火到网友自己剪合集、玩梗，可真打开游戏，你会发现玩法和广告差了十万八千里。
还有品牌干脆拿 AI 制作擦边剧情的视频，把你一路吊到产品出场：
什么女生正在洗澡，搓澡大叔推门进来；两个男人在卫生间，一个女人突然闯入，举起蒸汽清洁机开始演示。
这些视频，差评君都不太想叫它们广告。它们不在乎你喜不喜欢这个牌子，只在乎你点不点进来，跟菜市场门口喊“走过路过不要错过”一个路数，顶多算个吆喝。
所以发生了什么，让当初能被大众记住十几年的广告退化成这样？
咱们不妨回头看，看看电视还是老大的年代。
那时候的电视广告就俩字：金贵。
1994 年 11 月，央视第一次公开招标黄金时段的广告位，山东孔府宴酒砸了3079 万拿下第一届标王，第二年就卖了 9.18 亿，冲进全国白酒前四。
到了 2009 年广电总局规定，每套节目每小时商业广告不得超 12 分钟，两年后又禁止剧集中间插播广告。
你想想，这种学区房级别的广告位，挤得进的都是大品牌，谁也舍不得拿烂片去填吧？
一条电视广告从构思到播出，按月算正常，按年算也不稀奇，很多经典就是这么磨出来的。
可时代总在变化。
移动互联网爆发后，大家看新闻、找乐子的地方从客厅挪到了手机上，广告也跟着搬了家。
2025 年，互联网广告占广告业务收入 66%
互联网时代有一个特质：每一条广告带来的效果，可以算得一清二楚。
倒是早期，大家并不太拿这些数字当回事。
2017 年 5 月，百雀羚发了一张民国谍战风的长图广告，在朋友圈刷了屏，光微信上的阅读量就有 3000 万左右。
有人对照天猫销量一算，转化率不到 0.00008，策划团队却回了句：一切强行谈转化的品宣都是耍流氓，我们就是想展示百雀羚太会玩了。
那会敢这么说，是因为当时品牌们都更重视长久的名声、更希望能沉淀出资产，信奉的是一种长期主义。
真要转化，就等一个好点子再发酵呗。
可惜，这份耐心在行业里没撑几年。因为我们进入了算法时代。
当大众时间搬进了短视频信息流，广告门槛就低到了地板。
能在大众眼前打广告的，从资金雄厚的品牌，变成了驾校、牙科诊所、小游戏工作室、短剧公司，还有放贷的 App。
当所有品牌都挤在巴掌大的信息流里，想让自己的产品被更多人看见，那么一定会出现一种趋势：
每个人都在自然而然地讨好算法。
其实这个逻辑和电视时代类似。
那会广告想被更多人看见，得讨一个好的广告位。信息流时代呢，就讨好算法。
算法的脾气很简单：一条视频有人停下来看、有人看完、有人留言，它就接着往外推；没人看，就把你压下去。
一句话，它既能让你一本万利，也能让你血本无归，看你会不会讨好了。
在这种生态下出现的广告，那本质就不是拍给人看的了，是给算法大爷看的。
好，问题来了，品牌方要怎么讨好算法？
视频平台的后台专门有两项数据盯着开头：2 秒跳出率和 5 秒完播率。
这两数据不行，说明你的话题网友不感兴趣，算法就不会推荐出去。
所以广告的头几秒，一定要不择手段地把人按住，闪电劈猪也好，热门剧切片也好，哪怕它跟你的产品没半毛钱关系。
按住了呢？还得让你看完，因为完播率也影响算法，那就搞点剧情吊着你：搓澡大叔推门进了女浴室，你总想看看下一秒吧？
看完了，你最好再留句评论，毕竟互动也影响算法。来吧，那就搞点有争议的话题，评论区吵得越凶越好。
几年这么卷下来，行业里就在比一件事了：
谁能用最少的钱，讨来最多的算法推荐。
你说你的广告有创意，能沉淀品牌价值，领导桌子一拍问你：那又怎样，人友商卖爆了，你卖几单了？周报怎么写？
你没办法的。
此时，ROI（投入产出比）成了广告人头顶上唯一的那个数。
在这个数面前，创意就不值钱了。
我们做个假设：老板让你给新车拍条 2 分钟的广告，你会花个大半年、100 万英镑，试拍几百次，把新车全拆了，让零件一个碰一个，从一颗轴承一路碰到整辆车吗？
你肯定不会。
开头两秒就一颗轴承在那儿滚，大家早划走了。第二天后台一看转化，你就完蛋了，N+1 了，算了，给你 1 就不错了。
但这正是史上获奖最多的电视广告之一，本田 2003 年的《Cog（齿轮）》。
信息流的出现，让广告进入了一个“性价比”时代，只看当下转化的时代。
既然只看转化，最省事的办法就是把管用的套路做成公式：开头一个钩子，中间一段狗血，结尾抛个争议，最后挂上链接。
对品牌来说，与其把宝押在一条精心打磨的片子上，不如拆成几千条便宜视频撒出去撞，总有几条能爆。
我有个朋友小 C 做短视频代运营，接了一家车企子品牌的信息流广告，1500 元一条，一个月做 500 条；剩下的活，车企还分给了另外五六家团队。
推算下来，这一个子品牌，每月就要发 2000 到 4000 条广告视频。
1500 元一条，在这行还算贵的。厦门有批专门量产广告素材的公司，业内叫“厦门帮”，单条压到 200 块；有了 AI 之后，连模特都省了，一条素材能压到 5 块钱以内。
这种几百到一千多的一条广告，你指望它们能到某个水准吗，给你来点原创吗？
不可能的。
小 C 他们做视频，都是直接找对标账号的选题文案，然后调成自己甲方的版本。甚至他们拒绝使用创意，因为创意代表着新，代表着没被市场验证过，那数据就不一定好看。所以创意，反倒是一种风险。
所以大家平时在做的，就是改编、二创、照搬那些玩梗的热门视频。
你想想，头上是 KPI 压着的，内容是要靠冲突和拼梗的、几千条广告是层层外包的，品牌方是根本管不过来的，坦克也是没有后视镜的。
那翻车就是早晚的事。
3 月，罗技旗舰店发文案说“当我一降价，你还不是像狗一样跑过来”；后来他们解释，是授权账号运营方的员工跳过审核发布。
6 月，滴露一条剧情广告的台词是“我可以不是第一次，但我未来的老婆不行”，后来滴露说是第三方达人创作的。
七夕，德芙官方旗舰店发布的广告，一个女生趁男友不在，跟暧昧对象分享了“德芙七彩礼盒”，对方开车两小时送过来。后来德芙被网友嘲讽为“绿帽巧克力”，德芙道歉说是第三方店铺运营团队创作。
你瞅瞅，这几条广告哪条中有实质性的产品种草，品牌宣传呢？都是奔着“有话题”去，有的可能是在玩梗，但玩得没有分寸，就是低俗和不尊重。
这就是为什么你我现在看到的广告，都像一种赛博垃圾食品，吃进去毫无营养，看多了更是让人觉得反胃恶心。
你说这些品牌吃够了亏，会不会长记性，老老实实回头追求质量？
吴修铭在《注意力商人》里提过一个循环，大意是每出现一种新媒介，先把它占满的，总是最便宜、最刺激的内容，等观众烦透了、开始抵制，行业才被逼着变好。
1959 年，美国读者早就受够了铺天盖地的硬广，结果 DDB 给大众甲壳虫做的“Think Small”不吹不喊，反倒自嘲车小，广告开始从吆喝变成讲故事。精品广告，很大程度上是观众逼出来的。
可如今的观众，很难再逼动品牌了。
大家确实比以前敏感，但忘得也更快。热搜的本质是一种遗忘机制，某条广告被点名批评，没两天就会被“明星塌房”“食品安全”之类的新词条冲走。
信息流时代千人千面，一个子品牌一个月几千条，你刷到的和我刷到的根本不是同一条，你吐槽的事情别人丝毫不知情，又该如何逼动呢？
所以对品牌来说，只要没出事就接着投；出了事，道个歉、甩个锅，是第三方授权干的，这事也就过了。还能咋滴，罚两百个欢乐豆得了。
品牌要卖货，广告追求转化本来无可厚非。
可当广告服务的对象从“人”转移到“算法”，当广告业永远只关注 ROI、只为数据而活，以后的广告业可能没有广告人了，只有投手；没有作品，只有素材；没有创意，只有消耗品。
各家守着各自的渠道，找人做效果广告，跟平台谈投流，一条不行就发一百条，就像楼道里的小广告，贴满为止。
当然，我不是说整个广告业都人心不古了。
平时我有刷到一些车企、手机厂商的品牌广告（具体名字我就不提了），他们也是在迎合算法，开头会来段有噱头的画面和台词，但整条片子的水准一点不含糊，给人感触很深。毕竟大家身处这个快节奏时代，你没办法硬着头皮对抗，但是你可以聪明地化解，不是非得为了算法就抛弃想法和本心嘛。
《广告狂人》第一季最后一集，柯达拿着一台新幻灯机来找广告公司，给它起名叫“转轮”。创意总监唐·德雷珀并没有解释参数，而是把灯关了，一张张放起自家的老照片，然后说这台机器不是飞船，是一台时光机：
“它不叫转轮，叫旋转木马。它带着我们像孩子一样转啊转，最后回到家，回到那个我们知道自己被爱着的地方。”
最后同事眼圈红着出了会议室，柯达也签给了德雷珀的公司。
那些“旋转木马”，那些让人记忆深刻、拍案叫绝的创意广告，如今依旧有品牌在坚持，它们理应得到更好的曝光和反馈，获得业内更多的尊重，这样才能让创意和品质回归主流。
一旦广告们彻底变成几小时生成一次的快消品，廉价，真就成了这个行业的常驻嘉宾。

articles.title: Geekom Fall tech week deals offer up to $730 off a new mini PC
articles.text:
Geekom has a ton of Amazon Prime Day deals with an array of mini PCs on sale for up to 28% off. Both Intel and AMD options are on sale, and Geekom hasn't restricted the sale to its older mini PCs; even newer Gorgon Point machines are on sale.
Check out this deal on Amazon
Geekom has 13 mini PCs on sale as part of Amazon's Big Deal Days event, and we're going to run over five of the best deals. As is the case with any PC right now, prices are elevated due to the cost of memory and storage. So, although the discounts aren't massive, saving any money on a PC right now is a win.
Geekom's newly released AI flagship mini PC is already discounted.
This sturdy aluminum-encased Geekom A9 Max (2026) comes with the AMD's refreshed Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 'Gorgon Point' processor, backed by 32GB DDR5, a roomy 2TB SSD, and Windows 11 Pro.View Deal
Headlining the sale is a 15% discount on Geekom's latest A9 Max Top AI, packing an AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX470 'Gorgon Point' chip. If you prefer Intel, the Geekom IT15 is 15% off, as well, dropping its $1,199 list price down to $1,019. This machine comes with a Core Ultra 9 285H chip, which has 16 cores (6 + 12), a boost clock of 5.4 GHz, and an integrated Arc 140T GPU with 8 Xe cores.
Out of the box, the machine includes 32GB of DDR5 SODIMM memory with support for up to 128GB, along with a PCIe 4 1TB SSD. This machine doesn't have two 2280 slots. Instead, it has an extra 2242 slot, along with a 2.5-inch bay for SATA drives. Of course, you're free to upgrade the drive and memory down the line if you choose.
A5 2027 Edition Mini PC: was $479 now $407.15
The Geekom A5 (2027 Edition) comes with a Ryzen 7 7730U processor, 16GB of DDR5 memory, and a 256GB NVMe SSD. View Deal
Digging deeper into the pile, the Geekom A5 is on sale for 15% off, as well, bringing its price down to $407. With a low-power Ryzen 7 7730U CPU and 16GB of DDR4 memory, the Geekom A5 is tailored toward lightweight web browsing or general-purpose office workloads. Of course, you can also ditch the stock Windows 11 install and use it as a low-power home server, as well.
This machine is limited to 256GB of storage and 16GB of memory, but both are upgradable. Like the Arrow Lake machine above, you get an M.2 2242 slot and a 2.5-inch drive bay alongside the main M.2 2280 slot (though speeds are limited to PCIe Gen 3 here). For memory, Geekom once again uses SODIMM.
The machine is built for low-power applications, with the 7730U clocking in at just a 15W TDP. However, you still get eight cores, 16 threads, and Vega 8 graphics, so you can expand into some other applications (such as lightweight gaming).
Air12 Budget Mini PC: was $395.1 now $284.05
The Geekom Air12 is a budget mini PC with an Intel Pentium Gold 7505 dual-core CPU, 8GB of DDR4 memory, and a 256GB NVMe SSD. View Deal
At the bottom of the pile, we have the Geekom Air12 for just $284, 28% off its list price of $395.10. This is as budget as mini PCs come, with just 8GB of DDR4 memory and a 256GB NVMe SSD. As with other Geekom mini PCs, however, you can upgrade the memory and storage. There aren't extra storage slots in this PC, however.
The machine is powered by Intel's Pentium Gold 7505, which is a dual-core chip with a TDP of 15W and a base clock of 2GHz. It'll handle light web browsing and office tasks, but not much else for a dedicated desktop. However, as a host system for a local file or media server, the CPU is plenty.
Geekom has more mini PCs on sale on its website, as well. The A5 Pro 2026 edition with a Ryzen 5 7530U, 16GB of memory, and a 1TB SSD is on sale for $569, down from $749.
The Geekom IT13 Max is a mini PC with an Intel Core Ultra 9 185H CPU, either 16GB of DDR5 or 24GB of LPDDR5, and either a 500GB or 1TB SSD. View Deal

articles.title: 微软提出“混合智能”新路线，协同本地 / 云端 AI 灵活处理 Win11 用户任务
articles.text:
IT之家 10 月 8 日消息，太平洋时间 10 月 7 日上午 10 点（北京时间 10 月 8 日凌晨 1 点）在美国旧金山举办的发布会上，微软提出“混合智能”（hybrid intelligence）理念，强调通过混合架构，结合云端 AI 与本地计算能力，在 Windows 11 系统上实际处理用户任务。
IT之家援引博文介绍，Windows AI 不再局限于单一的云端调用或设备端运行，会根据任务类型、设备性能和安全需求，在本地与云端之间进行协同：对隐私敏感、需要快速响应的任务，可更多依靠本地处理；对于复杂模型和高算力需求，则交由云端完成。
Windows 可能成为这一模式的重要入口：用户提出目标后，Copilot 和 AI 智能体负责理解上下文、调用相关工具并推进任务，同时保留用户对关键步骤、权限和最终结果的控制。
这一理念与微软此前提出的“前沿生态系统”相互呼应。微软首席执行官萨蒂亚 · 纳德拉将信任、智能以及“融入人类抱负的 AI”视为三大支柱，并把 Agent 365、Microsoft IQ 和 Copilot 称为微软的“关键支点”。
在这一框架下，混合智能强调重新设计人与 Windows、应用和智能体之间的协作方式。微软还提到混合架构和本地 — 云端协同的重要性：设备端可承担需要低延迟、隐私保护的任务，云端则提供更强的模型和计算能力。结合 Execution Containers 等受控运行环境，AI 智能体有望在获得必要权限的情况下执行更复杂的操作。
在本次活动中，微软高级技术项目经理凯拉 · 辛纳蒙演示 GitHub Copilot，它会自动选择本地模型，并非一股脑地调用云端模型处理。

articles.title: LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration for Constrained Multi-Objective Container Placement
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.07030v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Container placement in data centers must simultaneously minimize power consumption and maximize affinity preferences, while satisfying multi-resource capacity and anti-affinity constraints. Traditional approaches typically rely on fixed rules, which lack adaptability to dynamic cluster states and are difficult to extend for adaptive decision-making. On the other hand, meta-heuristic methods, although more flexible, are often computationally expensive, slower and prone to getting trapped in local optima. In this work, we propose an adaptive and efficient approach based on an LLM-driven multi-agent collaboration framework, where four specialized agents operate in a closed-loop ReAct cycle at each placement step. A Power Consumption Agent and an Affinity Agent debate over competing objectives, while a Placement Agent resolves conflicts using Tolerance-Gated Arbitration (TGA). A Rearrangement Agent further refines decisions through the Monotone Improvement Rule (MIR) in a post-placement refinement phase. All the agents reason over deterministic, feasibility-filtered candidate tables provided by the environment, ensuring that every proposed action inherently satisfies hard constraints. Based on experimental evaluation using the Google Cluster Trace with a configuration of 100 applications and 25 machines, the proposed framework consumes 8.36% less power and achieves 39.30% higher affinity than the power-greedy baseline. Ablation studies confirm that each architectural component, the multi-round debate mechanism, the TGA in the Placement Agent, and the MIR in the Rearrangement Agent, contributes meaningfully to the overall performance, with removal of any single component degrading both power consumption and affinity satisfaction.

articles.title: Claude、GPT“跨界”做视频，Seedance们的护城河还牢吗？
articles.text:
（本文作者为 AI价值官，钛媒体经授权发布）
文 | AI价值官，作者丨星野，编辑丨美圻
过去一个月，AI视频领域最激动人心的讨论热潮，并非围绕Seedance、Minmax、可灵等专业视频模型，而是“越界”闯入的通用大模型。
Claude Opus 5.5 靠代码渲染视频，短短数日内催生出大量科普动画、创意短片和音乐MV，在X等平台涌现出多条爆款，甚至带火了一种新的创作范式：Vibe Video。
GPT-6 Astra则扮演起了“AI导演”，从分镜规划做到白模预演，通过深入 Blender、Unreal Engine、DaVinci Resolve 等专业软件，承担场景搭建、镜头预演、剪辑执行等工作，逐渐开始占据视频生成的上游。
两者走的是截然不同的两条路：一条是代码渲染的程序化创意，一条是空间规划的影视工业化。它们都没有在画质上正面硬刚，却从上游入口和细分场景切入，悄悄改写着AI视频的能力边界。
就在通用大模型从外围跨界切入、悄然改写AI视频能力边界的同时，专业视频模型的布局也在加速推进。字节、MiniMax、快手等头部玩家集体向创作上游渗透，逐步覆盖脚本拆解、分镜调度、成片剪辑的完整生产链路。这种对创作全流程的深度扎根，让它们在这轮跨界冲击之中，具备了更强的不可替代性。
Opus 5.5带火Vibe Video，代码直接“画”出视频？
9月22日，Anthropic 正式发布 Claude Opus 5.5。官方将发布重心放在编程能力与 Agent 任务执行上，视频能力并不是产品发布的主角。但在随后的开发者测试中，意外的爆点悄然出现：这款模型虽不直接输出像素画面，却能通过编写前端代码，生成完成度极高的动画视频。
这并非全新思路。此前 “SVG 画鹈鹕骑自行车” 一类的纯代码绘图测试早已在社区流传。但 Opus 5.5的代码稳定性与任务规划能力，让这种创作方式从玩具级演示走向了全面落地，相关作品先在X平台集中涌现，随后蔓延至小红书、抖音等国内平台。
有创作者调侃，Opus 5.5发布后的一周，自己的时间线几乎被各类AI代码视频填满。
热潮之中，最具破圈效应的标杆案例来自X平台博主 @anabology。他仅向 Opus 5.5 提供了一段参考提示词、Midjourney 调用权限与一份情绪板，模型便自主启动全流程制作，12小时后便输出了一部电影质感的反乌托邦短片。截至目前，该作品相关帖子的浏览量已突破2000万。
马斯克对这条作品表现出极高关注度，先后多次转发互动，直言 “这一次我真切感受到了AGI的深远影响”。他还对一条“Opus 5.5已达到通用人工智能80%-90%水平” 的观点帖回复 “Accurate”。来自直接竞争对手的公开认可，让 Opus 5.5的视频能力进一步破圈。
科普短片、产品宣传片等场景也涌现出了大量引爆讨论的案例。博主vittorio仅给出一句创作指令，Opus 5.5 便产出一部2分16秒的西方文明史短片，全片未调用任何专业视频生成模型。视频发布两天播放量破千万。
有创作者依托Opus 5.5基于Remotion框架编写约7400行前端代码，自动完成全片画面动效与转场节奏编排，搭配开源语音与Python生成的配乐，仅一小时就产出一支三分钟的AI发展史主题视频。
推理初创公司Deedy使用Opus 5.5制作产品发布视频，单条视频生成耗时仅约 1 分钟，API 成本仅约2美元，最终收获32万播放量。Wasmer团队则直接将产品发布公告的文字内容输入Opus 5.5，模型便一次性生成了完整的品牌宣传视频，传播效果超出团队预期。
这些案例让“Vibe Video” 迅速成为一种新的创作范式：不依赖专业视频模型，仅凭大模型写代码，就能产出完整视频。GitHub上的案例集合站awesome-opus5-5-videos已收录400多条作品，覆盖动效图形、知识讲解、3D 场景、小游戏等品类，每条都附有创作者公开的原始提示词与代码，相当于把成熟的创作方法论直接开源。国内创作者也纷纷入场，用它制作产品宣传片、科普动画和数据可视化视频。
Opus 5.5 的视频生成逻辑，与传统视频生成模型有着本质区别。
传统模型基于海量训练素材一次性生成完整画面，Claude走的是纯代码渲染路线，像专业动效设计师一样逐帧搭建画面——通过编写 SVG、Canvas、Three.js、Remotion等前端代码定义所有视觉元素与运动轨迹，再在无头浏览器中运行并逐帧录制，最终经 FFmpeg编码合成MP4文件，过程中还会自动校验帧画面并修正偏差。
整个流程里，大模型一人分饰四角：担任导演敲定分镜节奏与视觉风格，担任制片拆解任务、调度多段代码并行生成，担任画师以代码逐帧绘制画面元素，担任剪辑完成音画同步与成片输出。
这条路线最大的优势，是极强的可编辑性与极低的迭代成本。传统视频模型一旦结果不满意，往往只能修改提示词、整条重生成；代码生成的视频则只需改动对应镜头的几行代码，参数、运动、风格均可精确控制，画面元素还能分层拆解。
但Opus 5.5的应用场景边界也十分清晰。它天然擅长程序化、图形化的内容，如文字动效、数据图表、科普动画和抽象3D场景，却很难胜任写实真人画面与复杂的自然物理效果，而后者恰是传统视频模型的核心主场。
这也决定了当前Vibe Video的渗透范围仍集中在轻量化商业内容、知识科普与创意实验赛道，尚未切入影视级写实内容的主流市场。
GPT-6 Astra抢走导演椅，视频模型将沦为“渲染工”？
如果说Opus 5.5是从代码切入创意视频，GPT-6 Astra则把手伸向了更上游的策划环节，重塑AI视频的生产逻辑。它同样不直接生成最终画面，而是扮演“导演+制片” 的角色：先完成创意规划、空间设计与镜头调度，再交给专业视频模型渲染。
GPT-6 Astra于9月3日正式发布，官方定位为新一代通用智能体模型，核心能力覆盖计算机操作、编程、科学研究等领域，其中对 Blender、Unreal Engine 等三维创作软件的操作能力，成为它切入视频创作的关键支点。
Higgsfield AI公开的一项测试颇具代表性。任务是制作一段连续穿越多个空间的一镜到底动画，Astra没有直接出图，而是先在Blender里用简单几何体搭起白模场景，规划人物走位和整条运镜路线，待空间逻辑与机位运动确认无误，才交给Seedance 2.5渲染成片。
最终成片里，镜头从一个空间穿入下一个空间，人物位置与场景关系始终保持一致，在相当程度上缓解了AI视频长期存在的空间错乱和镜头穿模问题。
Astra的全流程创作能力同样引人注目。海外创作者Nate Herk做过一个实验：只给一句开放式指令，让Astra制作一条关于自身发布的YouTube视频。Astra 自主完成资料调研与脚本撰写，调用工具生成克隆声音旁白，驱动AI数字人出镜，并完成素材剪辑与音乐音效搭配，最终交出可直接发布的成片。
专业剪辑软件的接入，进一步放大了这种能力。9月8日，DaVinci Resolve 21.1上线原生MCP服务器，支持AI助手通过协议直接操作软件。一位拥有20 年经验的剪辑师把75分钟的原始素材交给Astra，它直接操作剪辑软件，输出了包含96个剪辑片段、字幕、调色与音量校准的22分钟粗剪版本，全程无需人工干预。
国内创作者也很快摸索出本土化的工作流。有人把完整的仙侠剧本交给Astra拆解分镜、设计镜头，再对接Seedance 2.5生成90秒成片，阵法设计与镜头切换的完成度超出预期；另有创作者总结出一套相对成熟的产品宣传片流程：先由 GPT-6做白模预演，验证镜头可行性，再导出预演视频交给视频模型渲染，最后用剪辑工具合成。整套流程约两小时，成本折合人民币仅150元。
支撑这些表现的，是GPT-6 Astra的世界模型与3D空间理解能力。它能理解多个相连空间的拓扑关系、人物走位的内在逻辑以及摄像机的运动路径，而不只是生成一张张平面画面。
更大的价值在于，创意因此变成了可修改、可复用的资产：空间布局、人物调度与摄像机路线都能留存下来，更换人物、场景、画风甚至故事时，不必从零开始。
至此，通用大模型已走出两条差异化路线，与专业视频模型构成交错竞争的格局。以 Opus 5.5为代表的代码派，长于程序化创意与动效科普，成本低、迭代快，适合轻量化商业内容。
以 GPT-6 Astra为代表的规划派，长于复杂镜头调度与空间叙事，搭配视频模型可产出影视级内容，更接近专业制作流程。二者并非替代关系，完全可以协同：GPT-6 负责分镜规划，视频模型负责写实部分的渲染，拼成一条互补的工作流。
视频模型集体跑向上游，全链路布局加固护城河
两条跨界路径，正在悄悄重构AI视频行业的利益分配。
一方面，产品宣传片、知识科普、数据可视化等商业与创意内容，开始Claude低成本的代码路线分流。另一方面，GPT开始掌握视频生成分工，将Seedance等视频模型降格下游的渲染工序，长期或将压低其在产业链上的价值。
就在通用大模型从外围搅动赛道之际，Seedance、可灵、MiniMax等专业视频模型厂商也在按自己的节奏加固护城河。各家方向高度一致：向上游创作环节延伸，深度嵌入创作者的完整工作流，用端到端的生产能力取代单点的素材生成能力。
9月20日，剪映在“AI新创作发布会” 上推出一站式创作工作台“剪映Hub” 和智能创作 Agent “剪映助手”。结合此前推出的小云雀Agent、内测的“漫剧创作工具”，字节已搭起“底层模型+垂直场景Agent+通用创作工作台” 的完整生态，用户从产生想法到导出成片，可在字节体系内一站完成。
其他头部玩家也在加速跟进。7月31日，MiniMax发布新一代多模态视频模型 H3。不到三周后的8月20日，便上线创作Agent工作台MiniMax Design，由主 Agent 拆解需求，调度多智能体并行完成从脚本到成片的全流程。
快手则在9月底亮出双轨布局。一边，可灵AI 4.0官宣10月上线，补齐30秒原生时长、4K HDR、多模态参考等关键参数短板，继续夯实模型层的竞争力；另一边，创作Agent工具ikli的内测消息同步流出，主打从需求理解、脚本编写到镜头生成、配音剪辑的全流程制作。
从结果看，这一轮全链路升级让专业视频模型的护城河更深了。大模型的长处在于创意发散、代码生成与流程调度，但在核心商业创作场景中，创作者要的不止是把想法落地，还有稳定的画质、标准化的成片质感、可复用的素材资产，以及与既有工作流的无缝衔接，而这些正是专业厂商深耕的领域。
叠加全链路Agent的加持，专业视频模型在短剧、漫剧、品牌广告等核心赛道上，短期内仍有难以替代的价值。
换言之，大模型带来的是新的技术路径与创作思路，拓宽了AI视频的边界，却尚未撼动专业视频模型的基本盘。
恰恰因为看清了上游入口的分量，字节、快手等才加快了全链路布局的步伐：只有深度嵌入创作者的完整工作流，覆盖从创意到交付的每一个环节，才能真正守住用户入口，不被架空为单纯的算力供应商。
通用大模型与专业视频模型的边界正在模糊，未来的胜负手，不在于谁的参数更高，而在于谁能更深地融入真实的创作生产流程，成为创作者离不开的生产工具。

articles.title: TRANSIT: Transparent Scale-in for Multi-Node LLM Training
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.07593v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: TRANSIT is a transparent scale-in framework to enable multi-node model training on fewer GPUs while maintaining training efficiency by transparently leveraging CPU DRAM as an extension of GPU memory during distributed training. It achieves this through a user-space interposition layer, requiring no modifications to the application, training framework, cluster scheduler, device driver, or operating system. Furthermore, TRANSIT achieves higher efficiency by leveraging a zero-copy data path for CPU-GPU transfers. We evaluate TRANSIT on dense and MoE models across scales up to 64 NVIDIA H100 GPUs and multiple parallelism configurations over a RoCE network. Our evaluation shows that TRANSIT can: (a) outperform state-of-the-art framework-managed offloading techniques, achieving up to 68%, 59%, and 42% higher per-GPU throughput than TorchTitan, ZeRO-Offload, and ZeRO-Infinity, respectively, (b) enables training with 50% fewer GPUs while maintaining over 90% of baseline per-GPU throughput, (c) lower per-node network traffic by up to 33%, and (d) improve per-GPU throughput by up to 35% in communication-bound settings.

articles.title: 好产品也会丢单，Palantir 旧访谈翻红：企业级 AI 订单，拼的不只是模型
articles.text:
Alexandr Wang 在 2024 年 12 月的一次播客访谈，最近在中文科技社群重新流传。
访谈由风投社群 South Park Commons 组织，当时他还是 Scale AI 的创始人兼 CEO，半年之后才加入 Meta 担任首席 AI 官。主持人问他，做产品和做销售怎么平衡。他的回答里有一句话被反复转发：在大型组织和政府客户那里，人们对一件事的认知，有时比客观情况更能左右决策。
他接着举了 Palantir 的例子。这家以美国军方、政府和大型企业为客户的公司，被他形容为一家剧团加软件公司的混合体，甚至长期给新员工发一本表演书。过去两年，Palantir 的市值从 2024 年 10 月突破千亿美元，到 2025 年 11 月最高突破 4900 亿美元，目前回落到 4500 亿美元上下。这段话随之被当成它增长故事的一把钥匙流传开来。
一本即兴表演手册
翻红的改写版本把重点放在“认知塑造”上，有的版本直接写成了教工程师“走进会议室第一秒接管客户大脑”的话术。Palantir 自己公开的交付流程里写的是：工程师住进客户现场，系统在客户自己的数据上跑起来，然后签订订单。
表演书的说法有一份第一手记录，在 Palantir 工作了八年的 Nabeel Qureshi，2024 年 10 月发表长文《Reflections on Palantir》，写到他任职期间新人入职会收到几本书，其中一本是 Keith Johnstone 的《Impro》，一本讲即兴表演的著作。
按他的理解，这本书用在客户现场，观察人和人互动时的地位信号，听懂客户的语言，工程师才拿得到信任，把数据整合和软件部署推进下去。这本书现在是否还在发，Qureshi 说他不确定。
Wang 用剧团来指 Palantir 面对客户状态。他说，在大型组织和政府客户那里，一家公司在客户眼里是什么样，有时比产品本身更能左右决策，Palantir 就是例子。他称这套塑造客户认知的做法为“黑暗的艺术”，前提是先把产品做好，交付真实的价值，这是底线，离开它，其余都不成立。
真正难复制的是驻场工程
把 Palantir 的增长归因于表演课，相当于忽略了这套打法里最难复制的部分。
Palantir 从 2003 年起为美国情报机构做数据分析。客户说不清自己要什么，数据散落在多个系统里，标准软件产品的形态在这里失效。工程师只能进驻现场，在对方的数据和流程里把系统做出来。这个角色后来有了正式的名字，Forward Deployed Engineer，前线部署工程师。行业复盘材料显示，直到 2016 年，Palantir 的前线部署工程师数量一度超过产品工程师。
这套打法如今有了标准化的入口，Palantir 官方给 AIP Bootcamp 定下的目标是五天：客户带着自己的数据和场景来，五天内在软件里搭出初步的使用案例。
官网挂出的客户证言里，Walgreens 借助 Foundry 和 AIP，八个月里把试点从 10 家店推到约 4000 家；AT&T 的 Foundry 上跑着 660 个应用，其中 S.C.O.U.T. 一个应用背后有超过 100 名 AT&T 工程师参与。财务数字是同一个模式的产物，Palantir 2026 年一季度总收入同比增长 85%，美国商业收入增长 133%。
信任在这里被拆成了可以逐项验证的步骤，客户不需要相信销售的说辞，五天工作坊里看到的是自己的数据怎么被读取，自己的流程怎么被搬进软件。权限怎么设，出错谁审批，审计记录留在哪里，Palantir 的治理文档里都有对应的工具。订单签下来之前，客户已经亲手验证过。
模型公司开始学 Palantir
OpenAI 今年 5 月 11 日宣布成立 OpenAI Deployment Company，一家由 OpenAI 控股的独立部署公司，启动资金超过 40 亿美元，来自 TPG 领投的 19 家机构，同时宣布收购总部位于爱丁堡的 Tomoro，一次性带入约 150 名前线部署工程师。
OpenAI 的招聘页面上，金融、医疗等行业单列 FDE 岗位，职位描述写明工程师要嵌入客户组织，把模型能力变成可审计、可交付的生产系统。
Anthropic 的做法是双线的，一边在官网公告与 IT 服务商 DXC 达成多年期合作，由 DXC 通过 Anthropic 的认证体系培训数万名 Claude 前线部署工程师，把他们送进银行、航空、保险和政府机构现有的 IT 系统；一边在自己的招聘页面上招募驻场 FDE，年薪区间 28 万到 32 万美元。据此前报道，Anthropic 还在筹备类似的部署合资实体。
麻省理工 NANDA 项目 2025 年的报告测算，95% 的企业生成式 AI 试点没有产生可量化的业务收益，问题大多出在部署环节。模型能力的差距在收窄，能把模型装进客户流程里的组织，稀缺程度在上升。
国内 To B 市场卡在同一个环节。采购方在签字之前要回答出了问题谁负责，能不能在自己的数据上验证，系统接进现有流程要动多大的手术。这些问题没有一项能靠性能对比表格回答。
Wang 那段访谈指出的问题，两年后仍然成立，即客户如何理解你的能力。Palantir 用二十多年的驻场工程给出了自己的答案，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 正在用真金白银抄写它。企业级 AI 的订单，会越来越多地交到那些把工程师派驻客户现场的公司手里。（本文首发钛媒体APP，作者 | 硅谷Tech-news，编辑 | 秦聪慧）

articles.title: AccentCL: Robust Accent Classification with Incremental Expansion
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.07426v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Accent classifiers are typically trained with a fixed label inventory and cannot accommodate new accent categories as new data becomes available. Moreover, accented speech corpora often exhibit substantial class imbalance and/or domain shift due to differences in recording conditions across corpora. We present AccentCL, a class-incremental learning framework for English accent classification that is robust to class imbalance and cross-corpus domain shift. AccentCL extracts multi-layer representations from a frozen Whisper-Large-v3 encoder, optimized with an imbalance-aware cross-entropy loss to reduce bias toward the majority accent classes and a domain mean alignment loss that minimizes distributional mean shift across training corpora. The label space is then expanded via replay-based continual learning, using the frozen base model for knowledge retention and an old-to-new margin loss to reduce overprediction on newly added classes. On a five-class accent classification task, AccentCL achieves 77.1% balanced accuracy and a 76.9% macro-averaged F1 score. We further evaluate the model's ability to incrementally incorporate two new accent categories: Spanish-accented and Chinese-accented English. When adding Spanish-accented English to the pretrained model, AccentCL attains an F1 of 83.3% on the new class while retaining 77.3% balanced accuracy on the base classes. When subsequently adding Chinese-accented English, it achieves 61.8% F1 on the new class while preserving 77.6% balanced accuracy on the previously learned classes. These results show that AccentCL enables robust regional accent classification while allowing new accent categories to be added without full retraining.

articles.title: AMD CEO苏姿丰：AI芯片需求强劲 将持续大幅扩充产能
articles.text:
快科技10月8日消息，AMD首席执行官苏姿丰（Lisa Su）预计，尽管芯片行业正面临AI安全等一系列挑战，未来几年市场需求仍将“非常旺盛”。
苏姿丰周二（10月6日）接受采访时表示，即便AMD持续提高产量，市场需求仍超过供应。她同时呼吁顶尖AI企业加强合作，确保这项技术不会造成危害。
苏姿丰称：“我们在2026年也增加了供应和产能，但可以肯定地说，需求甚至高于我们的供应。我们将在2027年大幅增加供应，但确实还需要更多产能。”
AMD的乐观展望进一步强化了AI行业的看涨情绪。此前，存储芯片制造商美光科技给出强劲业绩展望，服务器组装商鸿海精密的季度销售额也超出预期。
目前，AMD在CPU领域与英特尔等公司竞争，也是英伟达在GPU领域的主要竞争对手。上周，AMD宣布将以82亿美元收购AI初创公司World Labs，以增强技术实力，并有望帮助公司向客户提供多种模型。
不过，部分投资者日益担忧行业产能过剩、债务水平攀升以及监管阻力。对此，苏姿丰强调，AI“对世界非常有益”。她认为，AI不会像一些人担忧的那样伤害人类，但仍呼吁全行业加强合作，以确保这一点。
她还提到，特朗普新成立的“超级智能特别工作组”（Super Intelligence Force，SIF）是推动相关努力向前迈进的重要一步。
苏姿丰表示：“在安全和创新方面，我们还有一些工作要完成。我认为，其中最重要的一点，就是我们要作为一个生态系统共同努力。”

articles.title: 安卓最强Soc易主！三星Exynos 2700多核跑分击败高通超级至尊版
articles.text:
快科技10月7日消息，博主i冰宇宙爆料，三星内部测试了Exynos 2700，其多核成绩比高通第六代骁龙8超级至尊版高出9.5%。
据悉，高通第六代骁龙8超级至尊版的多核成绩在13000分左右。由此推测，三星Exynos 2700的多核成绩能够接近15000分，这将是安卓阵营最强悍的手机芯片。
公开爆料显示，Exynos 2700的核心升级主要集中在三个方面，分别是制程、封装与主频。在制程方面，该芯片将采用三星第二代2nm GAA工艺SF2P。相比第一代SF2工艺，其综合性能可提升12%，整体功耗降低25%。
根据此前披露的信息，三星SF2P工艺已在2026年1月实现70%的良率门槛，这为芯片冲击更高频率奠定了基础。
在封装方面，Exynos 2700不再沿用传统的垂直堆叠内存方案，转而采用名为Side-by-Side的新架构。该架构将SoC与DRAM并排放置，并在上层覆盖热传导块（HPB）。这一结构可以扩大SoC与散热材料的接触面积，消除垂直堆叠带来的热阻现象，从而进一步增强散热表现。
另外，Exynos 2700的超大核频率预计提升至4.2GHz，这将是三星史上最强悍的手机芯片。这颗芯片将由三星Galaxy S27系列首发搭载，而国行版和美版预计仍然会使用骁龙芯片。
消息称Exynos 2700的产量相比上代Exynos 2600提升了10%，这从侧面表明三星SF2P工艺的良率进一步提升。

articles.title: Samsung 9100 Pro SSD gets another price cut, up to 51% off
articles.text:
Amazon has gone absolutely rogue by slashing prices on the Samsung 9100 Pro again before its Big Deals sales event is over. We're in the last stretch, but the 1TB, 2TB, and 4TB models of this top-spec SSD are now cheaper than they were yesterday. The 4TB 9100 Pro has seen a huge cut, from $1,119.99 yesterday to $734.99 today, a price we've not seen in months. Elsewhere, the 1TB drive has dropped below $200, while the 2TB drive is now below $335, and the 8TB is staying steady at $2299.99.
This really is the best time to pick up one of these Samsung SSDs, especially if you want to upgrade your storage at a price that beats the current market. There's no guarantee that the stock will last, but we do know that these deal prices are set to go in less than 24 hours. These Gen 5 drives are still, somehow, beating the Gen 4 Samsung 990 Pro on pricing, making this one of the deals of the whole event.

Check out the Samsung 9100 Pro 2TB deal on Amazon
Check out the Samsung 9100 Pro 4TB deal on Amazon
Check out the Samsung 9100 Pro 8TB deal on Amazon
This is a brilliant SSD, no doubt about it, and easily one of the best SSDs you can buy. As our Samsung 9100 Pro review explains, this drive ships with Samsung's own Presto controller and 236-layer V8 NAND. You're getting max sequential reads and writes of 14,800 MB/s and 13,400 MB/s apiece, although speeds do vary slightly, depending on capacity.
At those speeds, however, you're not really hitting too many bottlenecks. This is a drive that can take the lot, from basic tasks to intensive AI workloads without much issue. That said, a high-performance drive in the current market isn't really the point. Price is the factor that you'll need to consider most, and so is the warranty, to ensure that you're protected if the drive fails.
This PCIe 5.0 SSD comes with a five-year limited warranty as standard, but it also has pretty good endurance specs, so it should last pretty well under tough conditions. The 2TB model, for example, is rated for 1,200 TBW. You'd need to be writing to more than a third of the drive every single day for five years to beat the warranty's coverage.

As specs go, the Samsung 9100 Pro is pretty much one of the best-performing drives on the market. You'll really notice the difference if you're upgrading from an older PCIe 4.0 drive. For instance, the Samsung 990 Pro, one of the best Gen 4 SSDs you can buy and this drive's predecessor, can 'only' hit read and write speeds of 7,940 and 6,900 MB/s, compared to the 14,800 MB/s and 13,400 MB/s here. You'll see even slower speeds at Gen 4, and below 600 MB/s with an older SATA SSD.
This isn't the fastest Gen 5 SSD, but that's hardly the point. The 9100 Pro is still a high-performance drive and, given these prices, almost impossible to beat on a cost-to-performance basis.Tom's HardwareTom's HardwareTom's HardwareTom's HardwareTom's HardwareTom's Hardware
Compared to the prices we saw yesterday, the 2TB model is even better value at just $0.167 per GB. The 1TB model isn't bad, though, as it drops below $200 for the first time in a while, and you're getting $0.196 per GB there. The 4TB model, meanwhile, sits in the middle, at $0.183, but that huge $385 discount on yesterday's pricing is difficult to ignore.
You can't go wrong with any of these high-performance Samsung 9100 Pro SSDs, though. You just can't wait long to buy one. These prices are set to expire by the end of the Amazon Prime sales event later today, but these SSDs could sell out before then. Grab one while you can, as time is running out fast.

articles.title: Leveraging a four-quadrant approach for evaluating Redpine Science
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.07937v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Redpine Science gives models and agents a single access point to a wide range of peer-reviewed literature, queried directly through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and an API. This report evaluates Redpine Science on two levels: the relevance of the retrieved chunks, and a model's answer when it has access to Redpine Science compared to web search. Both public and expert-validated benchmarks are used. Public benchmarks are a widely accepted way to test model development and are comparable across labs, but risk saturation and memorization. To address this, we complement them with an expert-validated question set. In total, this report presents four evaluations. On ScholarQABench SciFact, the public answer-quality benchmark reported here, an agent with Redpine Science answers 94.4% of claims correctly against 87.6% with no retrieval. On the expert-validated question set, an agent with Redpine Science states 80.1% of the required claims against 70.2% for an agent restricted to web search. On the 668 queries of a public retrieval benchmark whose gold paper Redpine holds, stripped of any model reasoning, Redpine Science places the correct source paper in its top ten results for 83.1% of queries (Recall@10), against 79.3% for the benchmark's creator. A blinded expert relevance panel places Redpine Science's Precision@5 at 75.2% against 39.8% for the PubMed search tool. We release the expert-validated question set and instructions to reproduce every headline result above, at https://github.com/redpine-ai/benchmarks.

articles.title: Memory-Efficient Expert Routing for Distributed MoE Training
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.07333v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: As Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models scale toward hundreds of experts and higher top-$k$ routing, memory efficiency in distributed training becomes a critical bottleneck. Peak memory is dominated by the MoE block, not attention: every intermediate buffer in the MoE dispatch pipeline is individually scaled by top-k routing. The standard all-to-all dispatcher sends all routed tokens in a single collective step, requiring the full top-$k$-expanded buffer to be constructed at once. In this work, we propose RelayMoE, a ring-based MoE execution model that computes locally as expert weights or tokens circulate, avoiding full top-$k$-expanded dispatch buffers. RelayMoE selects between expert and token routing according to communication volume and overlaps transfers with computation. The ring structure naturally supports memory-efficient MoE recomputation during backward: each hop reconstructs expert intermediates, uses them to compute gradients, and releases them before the next hop. The saved memory supports longer sequences and larger batches, or retains more attention activations to reduce attention recomputation and improve training throughput. We evaluate RelayMoE on 30B$-$57B production MoE models and varied expert configurations. In single-layer MoE experiments, RelayMoE achieves a $2\times$ average speedup over Megatron-LM. In full-model training under the same GPU memory budget, it improves throughput by up to $2.02\times$ and extends the largest tested trainable sequence length by up to $2.85\times$.

articles.title: When Robots Crash: Optimal Asynchronous Gathering at Weber Meeting Nodes
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.06939v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: We study the \textit{optimal gathering} problem over a finite set of designated \textit{meeting nodes} for \textit{asynchronous, anonymous,} and \textit{oblivious} mobile robots on an infinite grid under crash faults. The robots have global visibility and strong multiplicity detection, but share neither a coordinate system nor chirality. The objective is to gather all non-faulty robots at a \textsc{Weber Meeting Node}, minimizing the total Manhattan distance from their initial positions. Up to $n-2$ robots may crash permanently, and such crashes are indistinguishable from arbitrary delays. Existing approaches often rely on a designated robot to break symmetry, whose crash may block the remaining robots indefinitely. Instead, our approach enables every robot to independently select the same target from its snapshot, while target-dependent restricted shortest paths preserve the target as a \textsc{Weber Meeting Node}. We prove that, under strong multiplicity detection, optimal gathering is impossible from certain fully symmetric configurations. For all remaining configurations, our algorithm \textsc{CrashTolerantWeberGathering()} selects a unique common target, preserves its optimality throughout the execution, and allows non-faulty robots to progress without waiting for crashed robots, thereby guaranteeing gathering in finite time.

articles.title: Kurate: Scalable Scientific Quality Analysis
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.07306v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Scientific search systems can find papers that are relevant to a question, but they generally do not assess the quality of the evidence that those papers provide. We present Kurate, a system that uses large language models (LLMs) to assess the quality of published studies. Kurate uses both the paper and its related documents (e.g., the study's trial registration and protocol), and links each of its judgments to the passage of text on which that judgment is based. We applied Kurate to a corpus of 4,347 papers (3,913 of which report randomized trials) and scored each paper on 8 dimensions of study design and reporting: specifically, statistical power, causal identification, preregistration, selective reporting, measurement validity, analysis prespecification, reporting transparency, and conflict of interest and funding. Across the corpus, we found that papers most often exhibited issues with statistical power, selective reporting, and analysis prespecification, although average quality differed between clinical areas. When compared against expert annotations of 60 held-out clinical-trial documents, the information Kurate extracted matched the expert label in 221/242 protocol scorepoints and 294/370 results-publication scorepoints, with AC1 0.94 and 0.81, respectively. Using a well-reputed, high quality clinical trial as a worked example, we show how a single paper's overall grade breaks down into separate judgments, with each linked to specific evidence from the trial's registration, protocol, and published report. Together, these results show that large-scale quality assessment of this kind is feasible, and that it can be used to address meta-scientific research questions.

articles.title: AI's Simmering Question: "Where the F--- Is All the Automation?"
articles.text:
A new age of discovery and automation is here. Can you feel it? The leading AI companies certainly can. But you may not.
The rare slow news day gave us more time to marinate on the significance of OpenAI’s late-breaking announcement on Tuesday that its unreleased AI model had solved or made major progress on hundreds of significant problems in math and computer science. What does it mean for those of us who don’t exert much brain power on algebra every day?
It’s difficult to separate these huge technical achievements from more commercially driven announcements that just keep the AI money train going. And it wasn’t lost on me that Tuesday’s announcement, while groundbreaking, came amid reports of OpenAI raising more cash, and a week after its buzzy developer day mostly underwhelmed. Meanwhile, the latest AI craze—consumer agents—is starting to crash into the reality that a lot of websites want to block bots. And economists don’t see signs yet, at least in major statistics, that AI is making us more productive.
One question animating this phase of the AI gold rush is: How will companies convert raw, impressive intelligence into actual, demonstrable usefulness?
I witnessed the debate recently at the Midway, a dark auditorium near the San Francisco waterfront that often hosts EDM shows and art exhibitions. Last week, nearly 800 software developers filed inside for a conference hosted by Modal—not an EDM DJ, but a highly valued seller of computing infrastructure and software tools for developers.
Modal gave headline billing to Scott Wu, who used to be best known for his prowess in math competitions, before the coding agent startup he founded, Cognition, rocketed to a $48 billion valuation last month.
He stood on stage in front of a slide that read: “It’s time to be ambitious.” He talked about a near future where companies are full of “virtual employees,” which would “work on outcomes instead of tasks.” With enough data centers, memory and sandboxes, the industry would get there, he said. “Agents keep getting more and more capable. That’s the entire trend.”
And what gave him confidence for his call to arms was math. “The moment for me was the AIME moment,” he said, referring to the time last year when advanced AI models began reasoning well enough to outperform humans on the kinds of high-level math competitions he used to compete in. “That’s when I knew it was all over”—meaning, humans no longer claim a monopoly on intelligence.
I heard a different tone later that afternoon at the conference from Diogo Almeida, a former OpenAI researcher who described himself as “co-author of some of OpenAI’s greatest hits.” Almeida, smiling and wearing a pink fur coat on stage, spoke with the insider zeal of someone who had defected from a problematic country or religion and could now tell you all about it. He now runs TypeSafe AI, which recently launched a popular alternative to large language models called Jev.
“Where the fuck is all the automation?” he asked the crowd, before firing off a string of recognizable acronyms, at least to this crowd. “My TL;DR on the state of what is going on in AI is 100% of LLMs today are optimized for assistance with RLHF.” (For the uninitiated, the latter acronym is reinforcement learning from human feedback.) In other words, LLMs are trained to please a human in the loop, so they excel at assistance and fail at unattended automation.
At the same event I heard some of the most important AI leaders pushing for more automation among their software engineering ranks, even as they acknowledged it could be a tough change. They didn’t sound ready to let the machines take over, either.
“One area we’re pushing a lot more on is [to] think, what are the repetitive tasks I’m doing all the time? Why am I still in that loop?” said Cat Wu, head of product for Claude Code at Anthropic, perhaps the most AI-pilled company in the world. “A lot of automation gets stuck in this stage of being semi-automated. Claude does 80% of the work, and I do 20%. And you’re doing the tasks repetitively.”
And some software engineering leaders are still vexed more by taming humans than AI agents. Dax Raad, a prominent open-source developer who built OpenCode, said his company’s latest problem was that human engineers aren’t actually paying enough attention to code that AI is writing. “I’m just trying to figure out how to get my team to ask the right questions and feel bad when something goes out that they didn’t pay attention to,” Raad said. “It’s the age-old problem: how do you get people to care more?”
In Other News
• Elon Musk announced on Tuesday night that SpaceX’s AI unit will now use some AI models from competitors to power Grok Bot, signaling a shift away from relying exclusively on models developed in-house.
• Microsoft on Wednesday unveiled its latest effort to run AI in PCs powered by its Windows software, rather than running the AI in the cloud, which the company said would bring down costs for customers. More here.
• Anjney Midha, a former general partner at Andreessen Horowitz, along with former executives at Google, Apple and Nvidia have launched a company that aims to make it easier and more affordable for smaller companies or startups to access such compute.
• The U.S. Treasury Department said Wednesday it had fined the parent company of startup accelerator Plug and Play Tech Center, the first penalty issued under an outbound investment restriction program targeting China’s tech sector.

articles.title: Stabilizing language models under continual learning via condition-anchored distillation
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.06940v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Continual adaptation of language models can change their output distribution on prompts learned earlier, while retaining every old prompt-answer pair may be undesirable or impossible. We study condition-anchored generative distillation (CAGD): retain a small set of old prompts, use a frozen previous model to reconstruct completions and generation states, and match its predictive distributions while learning the next task. The formulation separates three roles that ordinary replay conflates: conditions select the behavior to protect, teacher generations locate relevant states, and soft targets specify how predictions may change. For autoregressive language generation, teacher-rollout distillation admits an exact chain-rule decomposition of sequence divergence. For masked-diffusion language modeling, our implementation directly controls local denoising drift on teacher-generated completions. In continual adaptation of a 219M masked diffusion language model, CAGD reduces four-task final held-out loss from 2.927 to 1.114 in one task order and from 2.168 to 0.891 in exact reverse. The same soft targets lower final average loss by 0.055 over hard replay when teacher-generated support is held identical. The direction persists on fresh facts and natural instructions across SMDM and Qwen3. On GSM8K, Qwen adaptation preserves answer-format compliance, but exact-match retention is seed-mixed at 0.6B and worsens at 1.7B. These results support condition-anchored functional preservation as a common design principle across the tested language-generation objectives.

articles.title: Component and Dimension Sparsity in Transformer Refusal Mechanisms
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.06903v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Activation steering manipulates large language model behavior by intervening on internal activations, but the mechanistic basis of these interventions remains poorly understood. We decompose refusal steering into component-level interventions across four open-weight models, identifying the sparse subsets of attention and MLP components whose steering suffices to reproduce the full behavioral effect. We find that refusal directions concentrate in sparse component mechanisms comprising 28--48\% of upstream components, retaining 88--101\% of steering effectiveness. Within these mechanisms, effective steering further concentrates in approximately 50\% of residual stream dimensions, retaining 85--98\% of the component-mechanism baseline, consistent with a privileged basis structure. Sparsity thus operates at two levels: which components are steered, and which dimensions within those components carry the signal. Together these findings show that refusal is not diffusely encoded across a transformer but assembled by a structured, identifiable mechanism, providing a foundation for mechanistic understanding of how refusal behaviors are represented and steered. To facilitate reproducibility, we release all code and raw experimental results in https://github.com/wang-research-lab/Refusal_Mechanisms.

articles.title: T-CCL: Resource Efficient and Performant Collective Communication using Tensor Memory Accelerator
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.07098v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Large transformer-based models increasingly depend on multi-GPU execution, which requires frequent collective communication among GPUs. Existing communication libraries often rely on many GPU threads to achieve high bandwidth or low latency, resulting in a large streaming multiprocessor (SM)-side resource footprint. This footprint can limit the resources available to other GPU work, particularly when communication and computation execute concurrently. Thus, efficient collective communication should not only achieve high collective performance but also reduce its SM-side resource usage. This paper presents T-CCL, a resource-efficient collective communication library based on the Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) for intra-node communication. T-CCL offloads both data movement and reduction operations to TMA and executes each collective as a pipelined series of asynchronous TMA operations, reducing the SM resources required for collective communication while maintaining high bandwidth. Evaluated across AllReduce, AllGather, and ReduceScatter collectives, T-CCL outperforms NCCL by up to 2.4x with unrestricted communication resources and up to 3.42x under restricted resource budgets, remains competitive with NCCL's recent symmetric-memory kernels, and occupies the same or fewer SMs in profiled cases. In a GEMM-collective overlap case study, switching the communication backend from NCCL to T-CCL raises the average operator-level speedup over a sequential baseline from 1.12x to 1.25x on two GPUs and from 1.04x to 1.14x on four GPUs, as T-CCL uses fewer SMs for communication, leaving more SMs available to the overlapped GEMM. Integrated into vLLM as a communication backend, T-CCL improves end-to-end inference throughput over vLLM's automatic backend dispatch by up to 1.31x, outperforming it at every evaluated batch size on both the conversation and decode-heavy workloads.

articles.title: Former Tesla Optimus Lead is Launching an Industrial Robot Startup
articles.text:
Ashish Kumar, a former AI lead for Tesla’s Optimus humanoid robots, has co-founded a startup developing non-humanoid robots that handle a variety of tasks that would normally be done by highly skilled workers in industries such as manufacturing and aerospace, according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter.
The San Francisco startup, Intelligent Machines, has hired several former members of Tesla’s Optimus team and is in the process of raising a seed round that could end up around $100 million, said one of the people.
Intelligent Machines is currently focused on developing software for robots, but its leaders have discussed designing the hardware as well.
The company uses reinforcement learning—a method that rewards AI for accomplishing certain goals and penalizes it for other actions—to teach robots to perform complex tasks, according to the two people. (Kumar’s doctoral research at the University of California, Berkeley, focused on RL.)

本法典彻底打破传统AI治理“重规则、无机理、无溯源、无落地”的短板，以NT1-NT4负迁移体系为核心判定标准、知识血统+铜脉接口双暗线为工程底座、七层递进架构为治理层级，实现从文字理论到可审计、可校验、可拦截、可回滚的工业级治理闭环，完成AI跨域治理从“经验约束”到“道统定规”的终极升维。
二、零号基准：全域唯一法定前置定标（000）
本集为全法典所有跨域负迁移场景永不迭代的唯一口径，定义四类AI跨域致命迁移原型，统一全体系判定标准，彻底解决行业语义混乱、定义模糊、判定无据的核心痛点：
1. NT1机制错配迁移：源域核心运行机制、底层逻辑在目标域完全不成立，是结构性底层失效；
2. NT2语义漂移迁移：指标、符号、概念表层一致，底层定义域、适用前提、真值逻辑彻底偏移；
3. NT3未知静默补全迁移：目标域空白项、未知缺省项被模型默认值自动填充，伪造确定性结果，属于静默隐形高危故障；
4. NT4权力偷渡迁移：源域隐含决策权重、审核权限、治理地位无授权偷渡至目标域，是最隐蔽、最高危、无监管的越界迁移。
三、七层递进核心架构（001-188）
全法典采用从微观事故→中观机理→权责制度→行业落地→顶层监管→文明维度→终局闭环的七层递进逻辑，层层锁档、逐级收敛、全域咬合，每层级终结均设置层基线锁档+术语永久固化，确保体系边界绝对固定。
第一层：迁移事故解剖层（001-021|21集）

第五层：跨域顶层监管层（110-136|27集）

构建分级监管、备案登记、强制上报、联合执法、熔断应急、风险保险、人才培养的全维度监管体系，界定行政处罚、刑事认定法理边界，建立国际协作、主权知识边境、规则迭代废止机制，填补全球AI跨域监管体系空白。
第六层：文明级迁移风控层（137-163|27集）
跳出产业与制度维度，升维至人类文明存续层面，识别跨域迁移引发的认知殖民、文化稀释、语义霸权、主体性让渡、自由意志侵蚀、代际不可逆影响、知识生态单一化等长周期风险。
建立文明韧性评估、知识公共资源保护、全球知识正义、碳硅共生契约、文明回滚机制，划定人类文明最小不可让渡底线，构建长周期、前瞻性的文明级风控体系。
第七层：法典终局锁档层（164-188|25集）
全法典自指闭环、终局定型核心，奠基九大公理体系，输出全域逻辑关联图谱，适配弱AI、AGI过渡期、成熟AGI三阶段治理需求。
统一法典迭代、评审、废止、反例纳入规则，形成司法、产业、政策、学术、媒体五大场景落地指南。
搭载三大可工程化审计工具集：迁移血统校验器、铜脉接口仿真测试器、NT负迁移自动判定机，实现法典从理论文本到可执行基准的终极蜕变。
最终锁定人类文明稳态基线、碳硅共生宪制约束，输出AGI时代跨域迁移治理终极适配预案。
四、法典核心优势与闭环能力
1. 定义绝对统一：000零号基准前置定标，NT1-NT4全域通用，彻底解决行业语义碎片化问题；

五、终审定稿状态

articles.title: 黄仁勋称英伟达因Windows而生：没它CUDA就不会诞生！
articles.text:
快科技10月8日消息，今天，黄仁勋出席微软举办的行业活动时公开发声，直接坦言英伟达这家企业最早就是因Windows生态而生。
黄仁勋在现场的对谈中提到，如果没有Windows这套普及度极高的桌面操作系统，就不会有后来的GeForce系列显卡；而如果没有早期显卡业务打下的用户盘和技术积累，面向并行计算的CUDA技术根本不会有诞生的土壤，后来带动全行业变革的深度学习大模型等前沿技术，也就完全没有发展的基础。
在英伟达创业起步的九十年代，整个计算机图形显示硬件行业正处在激烈蜕变的混沌时期，当时市面上玩家玩3D游戏的主流解决方案，都是单独配一张2D日常显示卡，再加一块专门的3D加速卡才能跑起来，两套硬件分开工作成本高、操作也麻烦。
当时英伟达敢为天下先，在1995年就推出了整合两路功能的NV1显卡，把2D显示和3D加速的功能全部整合在单张卡上。
但这款初代产品步子迈得太大，采用了当时行业里还非主流的二次曲面技术，完全没法兼容微软后来推出的D3D通用图形标准，上市之后销量惨淡，英伟达当时差点没能撑过初创期。
吃了闭门羹之后英伟达迅速放弃了此前技术路线上的偏执，主动向行业通用标准靠拢，在1997年推出了面向主流市场的RIVA 128显卡。
整个团队把微软D3D标准的适配优化放在驱动开发的第一优先级上，靠着单卡整合高性价比、行业里率先支持AGP接口的优势，这款产品上市之后迅速爆卖，直接让英伟达在竞争激烈的显卡市场站稳了脚跟。

articles.title: 三星HBM4e内存芯片拿到NVIDIA认证：48GB容量、性能提升20%
articles.text:
快科技10月7日消息，尽管在HBM2/3时代落后于SK海力士，但三星在HBM4时代正式翻身，不仅率先出货了HBM4内存，现在HBM4e也更进一步，被指拿到了NVIDIA的认证。
据韩国媒体报道，三星的HBM4e内存在上个月底拿到了包括NVIDIA在内的多家客户的产品资格认证，这个认证是针对产品质量验证的，不代表获得了各大客户的合同订单、供应量及量产时间。
不过三星官方针对这个消息的说法没有明确表态，称无法确认，但不否认的态度就能说明问题了。
现在的HBM4e内存规格也比之前的计划要保守一些，是12-Hi堆栈的，最大容量48GB，如果是之前激进版的16-Hi堆栈，容量能达到64GB，但良率和成本都会是更大的问题，NVIDIA都很难说用得起，Rubin这一代已经开始调低HBM规格了。
三星的HBM4e的内存芯片用的是第六代10nm工艺1c，基础芯片则是三星的4nm工艺生产，针脚速度达到了16Gbps，三星宣称性能比前代HBM4提升20%以上，通过低功耗设计和封装结构优化，能效提升了16%以上。
根据NVIDIA的计划，HBM4e内存会在明年出货的Rubin Ultra上正式出货，之前计划配备1TB HBM4e，但近期Rubin显卡规格都在调整，因此不确定性很多，最终规格还有待确认。

articles.title: FailBench: Evaluating Fault Tolerance Across Distributed Training Architectures
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.07688v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Distributed deep learning relies on data, pipeline, tensor, and hybrid parallelism, yet fault-tolerance mechanisms are typically evaluated only on the architecture for which they were designed. This leaves practitioners with little guidance when choosing mechanisms across architectures. FailBench provides a unified evaluation harness covering seven distributed training architectures, eight crash-fault-tolerance mechanisms and a no-FT baseline, and single, concurrent, and cascading fail-stop failures. We evaluate 142 (architecture, mechanism, trace) combinations on an 8xV100 cluster, with per-rank checkpoint states ranging from 205 MB to 2.7 GB. Three findings emerge. First, no mechanism is universally best: on A2, disk checkpointing has the lowest steady-state overhead (0.5%), in-memory replication restores fastest (~17 ms), and just-in-time checkpointing avoids periodic steady-state checkpoint cost but incurs ~0.9 s upon failure. When process-group re-formation takes seconds, mechanisms differ more in runtime overhead than restore speed. Second, gossip training increases sample throughput by 17.9% after losing a worker, yet shows no detectable improvement in loss progress over a matched no-fault baseline. Third, mechanism cost depends strongly on architecture: in-memory replication overhead ranges from 3.7% to 176%. We translate these findings into a decision framework for selecting fault-tolerance mechanisms and release FailBench as an open artifact.

articles.title: Visual Abstention in Unified Multimodal Models
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.07887v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) integrate understanding and generation, yet their generative behavior is rarely governed by what they understand about the task. We formalize visual abstention: when a requested visual transformation is impossible under the task's rules, the model should recognize that no valid solution exists, state this, and decline to generate. We introduce Draw-or-Decline (DoD), a benchmark of 1,050 feasible-infeasible request pairs across 7 task categories that jointly measures editing success and the refusal of infeasible requests. Evaluating 8 UMMs, we find that editing ability and abstention are distinct capabilities: even the strongest editor, at 68.4% editing accuracy, refuses only 0.4% of infeasible requests under ordinary instructions. Their reasoning shows why: the models rarely notice the conflict, and instead plan the edit as if the request were possible, often describing objects that are not in the image, or quietly change the request into one they can complete. Explicitly prompting these UMMs to report infeasibility increases textual refusals but reduces editing accuracy. We propose VisTA (Visual Transformation and Abstention), a training method that pairs feasible and infeasible examples so that a model judges feasibility before deciding whether to generate. We train VisTA-BAGEL to perform feasible edits and decline infeasible requests. Without any reminder, it refuses 93.0% of infeasible requests, up from 0.4% for the strongest editor, while falsely refusing only 0.8% of feasible ones. Unlike a reminder, this does not cost editing accuracy: VisTA-BAGEL completes 74.3% of feasible edits, more than any of the 8 evaluated UMMs.

articles.title: Identifying Introspection From the Inside
articles.text:
arXiv:2610.07186v1 Announce Type: new
Abstract: Large language models make claims about themselves that are both consequential and increasingly difficult to verify from behavior alone. How can we distinguish plausible confabulations from genuine introspection? In this paper, we identify mechanistic signatures of faithful self-report in a controlled setting. Using low-rank adapters, we train models to make decisions on behalf of fictitious characters, according to latent linear preference functions. We find sustained fine-tuning on an implicit decision task can lead to the emergence of accurate self-reporting of models' learned preferences, even without explicit self-report supervision. We ask two research questions about this emergent phenomenon. First: is the emergence of accurate self-reporting accompanied by a measurable structural change in the model? Weight ablations and frozen-layer experiments together indicate that preference representations shift to earlier layers over training, consistent with the hypothesis that faithful self-report requires preferences to be located where pre-existing verbalization mechanisms can access them. Second: can these structural differences distinguish faithful models from unfaithful ones? Using attribution patching, we find that faithful models exhibit significantly higher attribution similarity between the decision-making and self-report tasks -- a mechanistic signature of faithful self-report that does not require us to understand the content of the report itself. Previous work on self-report has observed behaviorally that models can be faithful or unfaithful; our work proposes that, at least in our restricted setting, it is possible to distinguish between the two patterns of computation by examining the structure of the networks themselves.

articles.title: 三星电子 2026 财年第三财季营收 195 万亿韩元，同比增长 126.59%
articles.text:
IT之家 10 月 8 日消息，三星电子今日发布 2026 财年（2026 年 1 月～2026 年 12 月）第三财季（2026 年 7 月～2026 年 9 月）业绩快报报告：
营业总收入：195 万亿韩元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 9668.1 亿元人民币），同比增长 126.59%，环比增长 13.7%。
营业利润：107.4 万亿韩元（现汇率约合 5324.89 亿元人民币），同比增长 782.5%，环比增长 20.01%。
AI 解读
本次三星电子 2026 财年第三财季业绩超市场普遍预期，核心财务数据大幅超出券商预测区间。
公司主营业务与财报核心数据
三星电子是全球领先的消费电子与半导体企业，主营业务涵盖半导体存储芯片、显示面板、智能手机、消费家电等领域。
单季度核心数据：2026 财年第三财季实现营业收入 195 万亿韩元（现汇率约合 9668.1 亿元人民币），同比增长 126.59%，环比增长 13.7%；营业利润达到 107.4 万亿韩元（现汇率约合 5324.89 亿元人民币），同比增长 782.5%，环比增长 20.01%。
累计核心数据：2026 年前三季度累计营业收入 500.37 万亿韩元（现汇率约合 2.48 万亿元人民币），去年同期为 239.77 万亿韩元（现汇率约合 1.19 万亿元人民币）；累计营业利润 254.13 万亿韩元（现汇率约合 1.26 万亿元人民币），去年同期为 23.53 万亿韩元（现汇率约合 1166.62 亿元人民币），同比实现爆发式增长。
业绩增长驱动因素
业绩大幅增长主要受益于 AI 产业爆发带来的高端存储芯片（HBM）需求激增，存储芯片价格持续上涨，半导体事业部利润贡献显著提升，推动整体盈利创下单季度历史新高。
机构评价与展望
当前三星电子股价在业绩公布前处于低位，机构认为本次业绩落地后股价存在修复空间，Mirae Asset Securities 给予目标价对应超过 46% 的上行空间。后续市场关注 AI 存储需求能否持续保持旺盛，以及消费电子业务的盈利修复情况。

articles.title: I bought this cheap $65 mechanical keyboard blind, and it ruined me for every other board I own
articles.text:
Sometimes you need a keyboard, and you need it now. That was where I found myself a couple months ago during local AI testing with one of the Nvidia GB10 boxes on my bench. Those systems are incredibly picky about which wired keyboards they'll work with for some reason, and moving the one known-good board I have on hand between systems under test was becoming a massive headache.
After one too many inconvenient keyboard swaps, I had had enough. I wanted a compact Bluetooth board that I could dedicate to my workbench, and I wanted it now. Testing on that GB10 system couldn’t wait, and I didn't want to get stuck in analysis paralysis. So I hopped on Amazon, filtered my choices down to items with same-day delivery, and found the Epomaker x Aula F75 Pro for just $65.
(Image credit: Future)
AULA
Aula F75 Pro Wireless Mechanical Keyboard
The Aula F75 Pro keyboard is feature packed with Leobog Reaper switches, dual-tone PBT keycaps, a volume knob, and wired, 2.4 GHz, and Bluetooth connectivity, among other features.
I was suspicious of this board at first, given the lack of in-depth independent reviews online and its unfamiliar switches. It uses Epomaker’s Leobog Reaper switches, which didn't map directly to any of the standard Cherry MX switches or their knockoffs that I'm used to.
But according to the spec sheet, they were linear and didn't have an incredibly heavy actuation force, which is the most important spec I look for in a keyboard when protecting my RSI-ravaged wrists. And they claimed to come pre-lubed, which is an upgrade I’ve never performed myself on any of my prior boards. So we were off to a good start.
The rest of the F75 Pro's feature list suggested custom keyboard DNA in its lineage. Spiffy dual-tone PBT keycaps with side legends? Check. A stack of noise-shaping and noise-reducing materials inside, including a cotton layer and a hefty silicone foundation? Check. A dedicated volume knob that doubles as a mute button? You got it.
Throw in wired, 2.4GHz wireless, and Bluetooth connectivity (with multiple Bluetooth pairing profiles), along with customizable RGB LED backlighting, and I was sold. And for such a low price, plus a few bucks extra for same-day delivery, I was willing to risk it if some aspect of this board wasn’t quite up to snuff.
A couple hours later, my Amazon delivery driver dutifully dropped the F75 Pro at my doorstep. And after a few minutes with the printed shortcut guide so I could pair it over Bluetooth, I had it connected to my GB10 box and was typing away in a terminal.
(Image credit: Future)
Despite this board’s low price, the Leobog Reaper switches underneath its keys are honestly the nicest I’ve ever felt. They’ve ruined me for every other board with MX-style switches I have. Whether it’s down to their pre-lubed treatment or inherent construction quality, they don’t have the tiniest bit of wobble or grit in their strokes like the red switch clones in many of my other mechanical keyboards.
The Reapers have a light 36gf initial force, a 45g actuation force and a 55gf bottom-out force, so they don’t place undue stress on my hands and wrists, and they have a nice, high-pitched audible “thock” at the bottom of their range that serves as pleasant reassurance for a successful keypress without rising to the level of a deafening click like blue-type switches might. The five-layer acoustic dampening stack within this board makes it the nicest-sounding one I own, too. And if I ever get tired of these particular switches, the Aula F75 has hot-swap support for easy modding.
I feel like I’m more accurate with these switches than I am with other boards in my office, and at 107 wpm with 99% accuracy on the MonkeyType test, I’m slightly faster than average on this board, too.
For all the thoughtful stuff that might be happening inside the F75 Pro's chassis, the outer plastic shell does feel a bit cut-rate. If you want the pleasure of knowing your board is clad in milled aluminum, carved stone, or some other exotic solid, this board doesn’t offer that satisfaction. But you're not touching the shell as you type. You're touching (and listening to) the keys. And I can attest that the tactile and auditory experience of typing on this board is far, far better than you would expect given its low price.
I also appreciate that most of the Aula F75’s functionality is available without installing any extra software. Although a utility is available, I’ve never felt the need to install it. I do have to refer to the included cheat card to figure out certain Fn combos, though, so don’t throw yours away if you get an F75 Pro of your own.
I do wish this board’s 75% layout dropped the volume knob for a dedicated Home key, but I can live with its existence on a Fn layer given the rest of this board’s virtues. And again, this board sells for $65 (and possibly even less during the current Prime Big Deal Days event). Given the hundreds of bucks that boards from big brands usually go for, I’ll enjoy what I hope is a long-lived and premium typing experience and keep the extra cash in my pocket.

articles.title: 半年净利暴增96%，重回中国台湾首富宝座，郭台铭靠AI赚翻了
articles.text:
（本文作者为 产联社CLS，钛媒体经授权发布）
文 | 产联社CLS
郭台铭靠AI赚翻了。
最新财报显示，2026年上半年，郭台铭旗下A股公司工业富联营收5578.6亿元，同比增长54.6%，创同期历史新高；净利润约237亿元，同比增长95.99%，首次突破200亿元。
与此同时，鸿海集团第二季度营收2.53兆新台币，净利润599.7亿新台币，同比增长约35%，创下单季历史新高。整个上半年，鸿海每股盈余7.84元新台币，营业利益同比增长65%，同样是历年同期的最好成绩。
最让郭台铭扬眉吐气的，是2025年8月，A股子公司工业富联市值一度突破万亿，将他重新推上中国台湾首富宝座。
提起郭台铭，很多人的第一反应依然是富士康。实际上，郭台铭的资产版图远不止于此，他一手创办的鸿海帝国，旗下拥有工业富联、鸿腾精密、富智康等约十家上市公司，横跨台湾、港股和A股。
那么，郭台铭卸任鸿海董事长后，为什么还能在AI这轮浪潮里赚得盆满钵满？这背后是一场怎样的资本与产业变局？
苹果代工厂，正悄悄变成 AI 算力巨头
如今，郭台铭旗下的公司，正悄悄变成 AI 算力巨头。
富士康是鸿海集团在大陆投资的子公司，是全球最大的电子代工厂，主要做苹果产品组装，TrendForce数据显示，iPhone 15系列有70%出自富士康产线；工业富联则主攻服务器，是全球最大的AI服务器供应商。
虽然公司体量足够大，但鸿海精密近十年净利润率始终是个位数，最高没超过3.5%，还有逐年下滑的趋势。竞争对手也在逼近：立讯精密2021年首次代工iPhone 13，如今已是iPhone第二大代工厂，2023年还从富士康手里拿走了iPhone 15 Pro Max三成的生产份额 。
改变局面的是工业富联。2026年3月10日，工业富联披露了2025年年报：全年营收9028.87亿元，同比增长48.22%；净利润352.86亿元，同比增长51.99%。这份成绩单，直接将其股价推上了历史高位。
2025年，工业富联云计算板块营收6026.79亿元，同比暴增88.70%。AI服务器业务成为绝对主力，云服务商AI服务器营收同比增长超过3倍。工业富联在全球AI服务器组装市场的份额，占到四到五成。
截至2025年底，工业富联总资产4562.24亿元，同比增长43.68%；上货币资金1100.25亿元，同比增长51.90%。
其实，早在2015年，鸿海精密将旗下通信网络设备、云服务设备、精密工具等业务打包，组建了工业富联。
2018年2月，工业富联在A股上市，从递交IPO申请到过会，只用了36天，创下A股纪录。同年6月8日，工业富联在上交所上市，募资271.2亿元，市值一度达到5000亿元。
真正的转折在2023年3月，OpenAI发布GPT-4，全球AI浪潮就此引爆，此时的工业富联手里正好握着一张牌：英伟达。
2017年，工业富联就和英伟达一起推出了全球第一台AI服务器HGX1；到2023年，双方的合作已覆盖产品开发、GPU模组与主板供应、服务器组装等环节，工业富联还是英伟达A100、H100板卡的独家供应商。
到了2026年，工业富联800G以上高速交换机营收同比暴增13倍，市场占有率稳居行业第一。
鸿海集团如今依然是全球最大的电子代工厂，是苹果最大的组装伙伴，但它同时也是AI服务器的全球最大供应商。
2026年的鸿海集团，已经在果链基本盘之上，长出了AI的第二增长曲线。
郭台铭的庞大资本版图
工业富联仅仅是郭台铭庞大商业版图的冰山一角。
在整个鸿海系资本矩阵中，除了承担AI转型核心使命的工业富联外，其余核心上市主体各有专精，补齐了集团全产业链布局的短板。
鸿华先进是鸿海集团进军新能源汽车赛道的核心主体，也是鸿海集团开辟第二增长曲线的关键布局。鸿华先进为台股核心上市平台，由鸿海与裕隆集团合资成立。
2005年，鸿海收购为福特、裕隆等车企提供汽车线束的安泰电业，正式进军汽车领域。多年来，鸿海一直为特斯拉、宝马、奔驰提供电子仪表盘、印刷电路板及塑料部件。
2020年，鸿海不再满足于做零部件，与裕隆汽车合资成立鸿华先进，切入整车代工。2021年至2022年，鸿海接连发布Model B、Model V、Model E、Model T、Model C五款车型。
与此同时，鸿华先进的业绩也在回暖。2026年一季度，虽营收同比下滑53%，但随后强势反转，5月单月营收同比大涨58%；7月营收达5.98亿新台币，同比暴增113.3%，增速实现翻倍式反弹。
如果说鸿华先进负责开拓新增长，鹏鼎控股就是负责给鸿海系提供稳定的现金流。
作为全球PCB龙头，鹏鼎控股绑定苹果、英伟达、华为等顶级客户，深耕高端精密电路板与算力硬件配套，是集团为数不多的长期高盈利核心资产，持续为AI、新能源新赛道赋能。
2026年上半年，鹏鼎控股营收172.17亿元，同比增长5.14%；归母净利润12.84亿元，同比增长4.11%。
除两大核心主体外，郭台铭以鸿海精密为核心，通过持续的资产分拆、产业整合、跨界并购，搭建起横跨A股、港股、台股的立体化资本体系。
目前鸿海系旗下拥有10家并表上市主体。港股有鸿腾精密，做高速互连、汽车电子、光模块；富智康集团，做非苹果品牌手机与物联网设备；云智汇科技，做工业自动化解决方案。
台股有鸿准精密，做精密模具与机构件；鸿海精密，是全球最大的电子产品代工服务商；桦汉科技，做嵌入式工业电脑；广宇科技与臻鼎-KY，做PCB与精密组件。
那么，这样一个横跨三地市场的万亿资本帝国，是如何造就的呢？
从10万新台币到万亿帝国
如今的郭台铭，即便早已退居经营二线，依旧手握横跨三地资本市场的庞大商业帝国。这个体量庞大的万亿制造版图，并非一夜造就，回溯半个世纪前，一切仅仅始于一笔 10 万新台币的启动资金。
1974年，24岁的郭台铭用母亲标会筹来的10万新台币，和几个朋友合伙注册了鸿海塑料企业有限公司。
而鸿海创办初期并不顺利。公司穷到连模具都买不起，于是郭台铭四处找模具厂借模具，好不容易才把生产搞起来。生产黑白电视机旋钮，是他接到的第一笔生意。
好景不长，不到一年，石油危机爆发，经济萧条，股东陆续退出，留下郭台铭一人支撑。他向岳父借了70万新台币，把业务转向电视机高压阳极帽组件。
1977年，郭台铭赚到了第一桶金，他拿这笔钱建了自己的模具厂，告别过去四处求人借模具的窘境。
但接下来的日子并不好过。有了新厂和新设备，却找不到合适的人才；好不容易凑齐了人，又没有足够的订单。
转折出现在1982年，郭台铭将公司改制为鸿海精密工业股份有限公司，投入上千万新台币建起规模化厂房，业务转向电脑连接器。
他跳过本土市场，直接去美国抢单。当时全球最大的连接器厂是AMP，同样的产品，别人卖1块，他只报6毛。靠着价格优势，他硬是从AMP手里抢下一批连接器大单。
这套打法，后来被括成八个字：“赤字接单，黑字出货”。赤字，就是账面上亏着本接单；黑字，就是最后落袋的利润。报价压得比同行低，先把订单抢到手，再靠死抠成本，把利润一分一分找回来。
1988年，鸿海营收突破10亿新台币，郭台铭做了一个关键决定：到深圳设厂。
那一年，他在深圳宝安成立了富士康精密组件厂，生产电脑周边接插件。后来他回忆，当时站在深圳龙华的一片荒地上，他说：“看得见的土地我全要了。”
此后三十多年，富士康在各地建起超过40个工业园区，公司规模也一路狂奔：2004年成为全球最大的3C代工厂，2005年首次入选世界500强，2006年宣布自己已是全球最大的代工企业。
从10万新台币起家，到横跨台、港、A股的万亿帝国，郭台铭用了五十年。如今，他手里最值钱的资产，已经从组装iPhone的流水线，变成了给AI服务器工厂。2026年，随着AI算力需求持续爆发，郭台铭的财富故事，还在继续书写。

articles.title: 蚂蚁阿福“科学减重1亿斤”迎来“退展”：中秋国庆假期全国60万网友胖了100万斤
articles.text:
中秋国庆超长假期即将结束，更“扎心”的灵魂拷问来了：你胖了吗？
健康AI蚂蚁阿福数据显示，9月25日-10月6日假期期间，全国参与阿福“科学减重1亿斤”的网友中，60万人累计长胖超100万斤。其中，超10万人长胖了3斤以上。
10月4日至7日，蚂蚁阿福APP的减重活动页面的统计数据，也已经连续四天显示“昨日全国增重”，10月7日显示昨日全国单日净增重达3.47万斤，被网友调侃减肥大业迎来了“退展”。
在社交平台上，此次减重“退展”也引起广泛讨论。有网友表示：“返工路上，不光心情沉重，身体也是肥嘟嘟的。”有人晒出体重秤照片，并配文：“阿福见证了我假期的鲜香麻辣，之后必将洗心革面。”也有网友“提醒”阿福：很多人还在返程路上没上秤，更大的“退展”在后面。
每逢假期胖三斤保守了？
这些省份减重“退展”居前
河南地区李女士告诉记者，她此前参与了阿福21天减重打卡行动，中秋国庆假期前往广东旅游，于10月5日返乡。“出发前瘦了2斤，回来一上秤，减重贡献变成了-2斤，”李女士说，“给全国网友‘拖后腿了’，广东早茶实在难以抗拒。”
李女士并非孤例。根据阿福公布的数据，在假期长胖人群中，体重涨了1-3斤的约27万人，大多数网友的体重管理“尚且可控”。胖了3斤至6斤的约9万人，已超过“每逢佳节胖三斤”的民间基准线；而胖6斤以上的有超1万人，网友自嘲“每逢佳节不是胖三斤，而是三公斤”。
从区域数据来看，广东、浙江、江苏、山东、河南位列增重省份前五。有网友表示，是不是美食大省，从增重斤数就看出来了。
不过，也有部分用户顶住“假期压力”，仍在为减重行动助力。中秋国庆假期，全国同时也有65万阿福网友体重下降，累计减重超100万斤。
假期长胖是客观规律？
专家和阿福支招节后体重管理
值得注意的是，“放假变胖”这件事其实已经被相关研究验证过。德国哥廷根大学农业经济学与农村发展系于晓华教授等人2020年在《应用经济学快报》上发表一则研究，根据中国健康与营养调查（CHNS）数据考察中国国庆假期带来的增重效应。结果显示，中国成年人在国庆7天假期期间的平均增重斤数为1.56公斤，也就是三斤左右。
减重科普博主、上海市第六人民医院普外科副主任韩晓东接受记者采访时表示，节假日容易长胖，与饮食、运动、作息等密切相关。假期里聚餐外食较多，高糖、高油、高盐食物的摄入也多，同时运动减少、作息紊乱，带来了体重增加。节后可以通过饮食控制与运动恢复体重。
对于假期长胖后的体重管理，蚂蚁阿福也提示：节后体重数字上涨，很大一部分并非脂肪堆积，而是水分滞留，一般节后3-5天体重会自然回落。建议节后不要一味节食或断食、恢复正常饮食节奏，可以用阿福的AI拍饮食管理每日总体热量摄入、营养均衡。同时，建议在一天中的固定时间（比如早起空腹）称体重，关注体脂率、内脏脂肪等多项指标，这样观测体重整体变化趋势更为准确和科学。
今年6月底，健康AI蚂蚁阿福发起了“科学减重1亿斤”活动，虽然中秋国庆长假遇到了“退展”，但截至目前，全国网友今年的累计减重斤数依旧有624万斤。
